nodes.name: Staircase S-matrix and TBA equations
nodes.statement: Trading the analytically-continued sinh-Gordon coupling for a real parameter $\theta_0$, the staircase S-matrix is \begin{equation} S(\theta)= \tanh\left(\frac{\theta{-}\theta_0}{2}-\frac{i\pi}{4}\right) \tanh\left(\frac{\theta{+}\theta_0}{2}-\frac{i\pi}{4}\right) \end{equation} and this leads to the following TBA equations for the pseudoenergy $\epsilon(\theta)$ for the system on a circle of circumference $R$\,: \begin{equation} \epsilon(\theta)=r\cosh\theta-\int_{{\mathbb R}}\phi_S(\theta-\theta')L(\theta')d\theta' \end{equation} where $r=M\!R$, and \begin{equation} L(\theta)=\ln(1+e^{-\epsilon(\theta)})\,,\quad \phi_S(\theta)=-\frac{i}{2\pi}\frac{d}{d\theta}\ln S(\theta)\,. \end{equation}
nodes.section: The staircase model, in the bulk and at the boundary
nodes.statement_short: Staircase S-matrix with real parameter theta_0 and the TBA equation for the pseudoenergy epsilon, with L and kernel phi_S.

nodes.name: Effective central charge
nodes.statement: The ground state energy of the system is then given by $E(R)=-\frac{\pi}{6R}\,c_{\rm eff}(r)$, where the effective central charge $c_{\rm eff}(r)$ is \begin{equation} c_{\rm eff}(r)=\frac{6}{\pi^2}\int_{{\mathbb R}}r\cosh(\theta)L(\theta)\,d\theta\,. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Kernel notation (x)(theta), phi_(x), phi
nodes.statement: For later use we define \begin{equation} (x)(\theta)= \frac {\sinh\left(\fract{\theta}{2}+\fract{i\pi x}{2}\right)} {\sinh\left(\fract{\theta}{2}-\fract{i\pi x}{2}\right)}~,\qquad \phi_{(x)}(\theta)=-\frac{i}{2\pi}\frac{d}{d\theta}\ln\,(x)(\theta)= \frac{-\sin(\pi x)/(2\pi)\,}{\cosh(\theta)-\cos(\pi x)}~, \end{equation} and also \begin{equation} \phi(\theta)=-\phi_{(\frac{1}{2})}(\theta)=\frac{1}{2\pi\cosh(\theta)} \end{equation} so that the staircase kernel $\phi_S(\theta)$ is \begin{equation} \phi_S(\theta)=\phi(\theta-\theta_0)+\phi(\theta+\theta_0)\,. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Staircase as union of MA+_m trajectories
nodes.statement: The natural interpretation of these results -- also backed by perturbative studies, in the spirit of \cite{Zamolodchikov:1987ti}, at large $m$ \cite{Lassig:1991ab} -- is that there is a one-parameter family of integrable quantum field theories with renormalisation group trajectories which, in the limit $\theta_0\to\infty$, approach the union of the renormalisation group trajectories of the ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$ theories. From now on we will assume this to be the case, and use it to deduce equations for the flow of the $g$-function in these same theories.
nodes.section: The staircase model, in the bulk and at the boundary
nodes.statement_short: Assume a one-parameter family of integrable QFTs whose RG trajectories approach the union of the MA+_m trajectories as theta_0 -> infinity.

nodes.statement: Further continuing to the staircase values of the coupling, this leads to the following reflection factor: \begin{equation} R(\theta)=\frac {(\frac{1}{2})(\frac{3}{4}-\frac{i\theta_0}{2\pi}) (\frac{3}{4}+\frac{i\theta_0}{2\pi})} {(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{E}{2})(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{E}{2}) (\frac{1}{2}-\frac{F}{2})(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{F}{2})} \end{equation} where $E$ and $F$ are two parameters whose relationship with the original two parameters of the boundary sinh-Gordon model will not be relevant below.

nodes.statement_short: Reflection factor of the boundary staircase model, the continuation of the sinh-Gordon one, with two boundary parameters E and F.

nodes.name: Exact g-function formula
nodes.statement: Its exact $g$-function should therefore be given by the formula proposed in \cite{Dorey:2004xk}. Explicitly, for a boundary at the end of a cylinder of circumference $r=M\!R$, \begin{equation} \ln g(r)= \ln g^{\phantom o}_{0}(r)+\ln g^{\phantom o}_b(r) \end{equation} where \begin{equation} \ln g^{\phantom o}_{0}(r)= \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{2n}\int_{{\mathbb R}^n}{\frac{d\theta_1}{1+e^{\epsilon(\theta_1)}} \cdots\frac{d\theta_n}{1+e^{\epsilon(\theta_n)}} \phi_S(\theta_1+\theta_2)\phi_S(\theta_2-\theta_3)\cdots \phi_S(\theta_n-\theta_1)} \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \ln g^{\phantom o}_b(r)=\frac{1}{2}\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\left(\phi_b(\theta)-\phi_S(2\theta)- {\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\,\delta(\theta) \right) L(\theta)} \end{equation} where $\epsilon(\theta)$ solves the TBA equation (\ref{stairTBA}), $L(\theta)=\ln(1+e^{-\epsilon(\theta)})$, $\phi_S(\theta)=-\frac{i}{2\pi}\frac{d}{d\theta}\ln S(\theta)=\phi(\theta-\theta_0)+\phi(\theta+\theta_0)$, and, restricting attention to the $n=2$ case of (\ref{Rn}) for simplicity, \begin{eqnarray} \phi_b(\theta) &=&-\frac{i}{2\pi}\frac{d}{d\theta}\ln R(\theta)\nonumber\\[4pt] &=& -\phi(\theta)+ \phi_{(\frac{3}{4})}(\theta-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\theta_0)+ \phi_{(\frac{3}{4})}(\theta+{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\theta_0)\nonumber\\[3pt] && {~~~~~}+\phi(\theta-\theta_{b1})+ \phi(\theta+\theta_{b1})+ \phi(\theta-\theta_{b2})+ \phi(\theta+\theta_{b2})\,.~~~ \end{eqnarray}

nodes.statement_short: Splits the single-integral term ln g_b into a phi/delta part, a theta_0-shifted part and a boundary-parameter part.

nodes.name: Equation (lngb1)
nodes.statement: \ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1} &= \frac{1}{2}\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\left(-\phi(\theta)- {\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\delta(\theta)\right)\!L(\theta)}\,,
nodes.label: lngb1

nodes.name: Equation (lngb2)
nodes.statement: \ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2} &= \frac{1}{2}\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\left( \phi_{(\frac{3}{4})}(\theta-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\theta_0)+ \phi_{(\frac{3}{4})}(\theta+{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\theta_0) - \phi(2\theta-\theta_0) - \phi(2\theta+\theta_0) \right)\!L(\theta)}\,,
nodes.label: lngb2

nodes.name: Equation (lngb3)
nodes.statement: \ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3} &= \frac{1}{2}\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\left(\phi(\theta-\theta_{b1})+ \phi(\theta+\theta_{b1})+ \phi(\theta-\theta_{b2})+ \phi(\theta+\theta_{b2})\right)\!L(\theta)}\,.
nodes.label: lngb3

nodes.name: g-function plateaux match conformal g-values
nodes.statement: In the large-$\theta_0$ limit, the full $g$-function passes through a series of plateaux as $\ln r$ varies, its value on each plateau always matching a (conformal) $g$-function value, or a product of such values, for the conformal field theory seen by the bulk theory at that value of $r$.
conclusions: the full $g$-function passes through a series of plateaux as $\ln r$ varies, its value on each plateau always matching a (conformal) $g$-function value, or a product of such values

nodes.name: Minimal model Virasoro representations
nodes.statement: The model has central charge $c_m=1-\frac{6}{m(m{+}1)}$, and the permitted irreducible highest-weight representations of the Virasoro algebra are labelled by pairs of integers $a$ and $b$ with $1\le a\le m{-}1$ and $1\le b\le m$ subject to the identifications $(a,b)\sim (m{-}a,m{+}1{-}b)$.

nodes.name: Highest weight h_ab
nodes.statement: They have highest weight \begin{equation} h_{ab}=\frac{((m{+}1)a-mb)^2-1}{4m(m{+}1)}\,. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Conformal boundary conditions are superpositions of Cardy states
nodes.statement: The most general conformal boundary condition is a superposition of `pure' (Cardy) boundary conditions \cite{Cardy:1989ir}.
conclusions: The most general conformal boundary condition is a superposition of `pure' (Cardy) boundary conditions

nodes.name: Cardy boundary entropy
nodes.statement: There is one such boundary condition for each irreducible highest-weight representation (\ref{hwr}), and its boundary entropy (or $g$-function) is \cite{Affleck:1991tk} \begin{equation} g(m,a,b)= \left(\frac{8}{m(m+1)}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}\frac{\sin(\frac{a\pi}{m}) \sin(\frac{b\pi}{m+1})}{\sqrt{\sin(\frac{\pi}{m})\sin(\frac{\pi}{m+1})}}\,. \end{equation}
conclusions: There is one such boundary condition for each irreducible highest-weight representation (\ref{hwr})
nodes.statement_short: One Cardy boundary per highest-weight representation (a,b), with boundary entropy g(m,a,b) given by a product of sines.

nodes.name: Cardy boundary entropy g(m,a,b)
nodes.statement: g(m,a,b)= \left(\frac{8}{m(m+1)}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}\frac{\sin(\frac{a\pi}{m}) \sin(\frac{b\pi}{m+1})}{\sqrt{\sin(\frac{\pi}{m})\sin(\frac{\pi}{m+1})}}\,.
nodes.label: gmab

nodes.name: Symmetries of g(m,a,b)
nodes.statement: Notice that this formula respects the identification $(a,b)\cong (m{-}a,m{+}1{-}b)$, and has the additional symmetries $g(m,a,b)=g(m,m{-}a,b)$ and $g(m,a,b)=g(m,a,m{+}1{-}b)$.

nodes.name: Z_2 spin flip
nodes.statement: This is the ${\mathbb Z}_2$ `spin flip' symmetry of minimal model boundary conditions which in the case of the Ising model maps between spin up and spin down Dirichlet boundaries.

nodes.name: Bulk near M_m
nodes.statement: Suppose the bulk theory is near to the minimal model ${\cal M}_m$, so that $\ln(r)$ satisfies \begin{equation} -(m{-}2)\theta_0/2 \ll \ln(r)\ll -(m{-}3)\theta_0/2 \,. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Alternating plateaux of L(theta)
nodes.statement: Setting $\alpha=2\ln(1/r)-(m{-}3)\theta_0$, we have $0\ll\alpha\ll\theta_0$ and, starting from $\theta\approx \ln(1/r)$, $L(\theta)$ exhibits an alternating series of plateaux of lengths $\alpha$ and $\theta_0-\alpha$, the $i^{\rm th}$ plateau being centred at $\theta=z_i$, where \begin{equation} z_i=(m{-}2{-}i)\theta_0/2\,,\qquad i=1, 2,\dots 2m{-}5\,. \end{equation}
conclusions: $L(\theta)$ exhibits an alternating series of plateaux of lengths $\alpha$ and $\theta_0-\alpha$
nodes.statement_short: With alpha=2ln(1/r)-(m-3)theta_0, L(theta) has alternating plateaux of lengths alpha and theta_0-alpha centred at z_i.

nodes.name: Plateau constants x_a, y_a
nodes.statement: Adapting slightly the notation from \cite{Zamolodchikov:1991vh,Zamolodchikov:1991vx}, define constants $x_a$ and $y_a$ by \begin{equation} 1+x_a= \frac{\sin^2\Bigl(\frac{\pi a}{m+1}\Bigr)} {\sin^2\Bigl(\frac{\pi}{m+1}\Bigr)}~~,\qquad 1+y_a= \frac{\sin^2\Bigl(\frac{\pi a}{m}\Bigr)} {\sin^2\Bigl(\frac{\pi}{m}\Bigr)}~.\qquad \end{equation}

nodes.name: Plateau constants x_a, y_a
nodes.statement: 1+x_a= \frac{\sin^2\Bigl(\frac{\pi a}{m+1}\Bigr)} {\sin^2\Bigl(\frac{\pi}{m+1}\Bigr)}~~,\qquad 1+y_a= \frac{\sin^2\Bigl(\frac{\pi a}{m}\Bigr)} {\sin^2\Bigl(\frac{\pi}{m}\Bigr)}~.\qquad
nodes.label: xy

nodes.name: Plateau values of L(theta)
nodes.statement: Starting from $\theta=+\infty$, $L(\theta)$ is close to $0$ until $\theta\approx \ln(1/r)$, and then has height $\ln(1+x_2)$ for $\ln(1/r)-\alpha\ll\theta\ll\ln(1/r)$, then $\ln(1+y_2)$ for $\ln(1/r)-\theta_0\ll\theta\ll\ln(1/r)-\alpha$, then $\ln(1+x_3)$ for $\ln(1/r)-\theta_0-\alpha\ll\theta\ll\ln(1/r)-\theta_0$, and so on, before returning to $0$ for $\theta\ll-\ln(1/r)$. In full, the plateau values of $L(\theta)$ are \begin{align} \ln(1{+}x_{a}):&~~~~~~~~~~~ z_{2a-3}-\alpha/2\ll\theta\ll z_{2a-3}+\alpha/2\,,\qquad~~~~\, a=2\dots m{-}1\,; \\[4pt] \ln(1{+}y_{a}):&~~~\, z_{2a-2}-(\theta_0{-}\alpha)/2\ll\theta\ll z_{2a-2}+(\theta_0{-}\alpha)/2\,,~~~\, a=2\dots m{-}2\,, \end{align} and the complete sequence between $\theta=-\ln(1/r)$ and $\theta=+\ln(1/r)$ is \begin{equation} \{ \, \ln(1{+}x_{m-1}),\, \ln(1{+}y_{m-2}),\, \ln(1{+}x_{m-2})\,, \ln(1{+}y_{m-3})\, \dots\, \ln(1{+}y_{2}),\, \ln(1{+}x_{2}) \, \}\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: L(theta) takes plateau values ln(1+x_a) on x-type intervals of width alpha and ln(1+y_a) on y-type intervals of width theta_0-alpha.

nodes.name: x-type and y-type intervals
nodes.statement: As a shorthand we will refer to the intervals in the set (\ref{platx}) as $x$-type, and those in the set (\ref{platy}) as $y$-type.

nodes.name: Padding the plateau sequence with zeros
nodes.statement: From (\ref{xy}), $\ln(1{+}x_1)= \ln(1{+}y_1)= 0$, and so we can formally add these two constants to the end of the sequence (\ref{Ls}) while remaining consistent with the values taken by $L(\theta)$ in the corresponding intervals, and likewise add $\ln(1{+}y_{m-1})$ and then $\ln(1{+}x_m)$ to the beginning.

nodes.name: Symmetry L(theta)=L(-theta)
nodes.statement: The symmetries $x_a=x_{m+1-a}$, $y_a=y_{m-a}$ reflect the more general symmetry $L(\theta)=L(-\theta)$.

nodes.name: Plateau values of ln g_0, ln g_b1, ln g_b2
nodes.statement: Then $g^{\phantom o}_{0}$, $g^{\phantom o}_{b1}$ and $g^{\phantom o}_{b2}$ are approximately constant, and given by the following formulae: \begin{numcases}{\ln g_0(r) = } \displaystyle {~}\ln\left(\left(\frac{8}{m(m+1)}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}} \frac{\sin\frac{(m-1)\pi}{2m}}{\sqrt{\sin\frac{\pi}{m}\sin\frac{\pi}{m+1}}} \right)&\mbox{for $m$ odd} \\[10pt] \displaystyle {~}\ln\left(\left(\frac{8}{m(m+1)}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}} \frac{\sin\frac{m\pi}{2(m+1)}}{\sqrt{\sin\frac{\pi}{m}\sin\frac{\pi}{m+1}}} \right)&\mbox{for $m$ even} \end{numcases} \begin{numcases}{\hskip -41pt\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}(r)=-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} L(0)=} -{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln(1{+}x_{(m+1)/2})= -{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln\left(\frac{1}{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m+1}}\right) &\mbox{for $m$ odd} \\[10pt] -{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln(1{+}y_{m/2})= -{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln\left(\frac{1}{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m}}\right) &\mbox{for $m$ even} \end{numcases} \begin{numcases}{\hskip -28pt\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}(r)= -{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} L\left({\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\theta_0\right)=} -{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln(1{+}y_{(m-1)/2}) = -{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} \ln\left(\frac{\sin^2\frac{(m-1)\pi}{2m}}{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m}}\right) &\mbox{for $m$ odd} \\[10pt] -{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln(1{+}x_{m/2}) = -{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} \ln\left(\frac{\sin^2\frac{m\pi}{2(m+1)}}{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m+1}}\right) &\mbox{for $m$ even}\,. \end{numcases} These results are exact in the limit $\{\,\theta_0\to\infty, -(m{-}2)\theta_0/2 \ll \ln(r)\ll -(m{-}3)\theta_0/2\, \}$.
conclusions: $g^{\phantom o}_{0}$, $g^{\phantom o}_{b1}$ and $g^{\phantom o}_{b2}$ are approximately constant
nodes.statement_short: On the M_m plateau, ln g_0, ln g_b1, ln g_b2 are constants given in closed form, separately for m odd and m even.

nodes.name: Equation (lng0fodd,lng0feven)
nodes.statement: {\ln g_0(r) = } \displaystyle {~}\ln\left(\left(\frac{8}{m(m+1)}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}} \frac{\sin\frac{(m-1)\pi}{2m}}{\sqrt{\sin\frac{\pi}{m}\sin\frac{\pi}{m+1}}} \right)&\mbox{for $m$ odd} \\[10pt] \displaystyle {~}\ln\left(\left(\frac{8}{m(m+1)}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}} \frac{\sin\frac{m\pi}{2(m+1)}}{\sqrt{\sin\frac{\pi}{m}\sin\frac{\pi}{m+1}}} \right)&\mbox{for $m$ even}
nodes.label: lng0fodd

nodes.name: Equation (lngb1odd,lngb1even)
nodes.statement: {\hskip -41pt\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}(r)=-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} L(0)=} -{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln(1{+}x_{(m+1)/2})= -{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln\left(\frac{1}{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m+1}}\right) &\mbox{for $m$ odd} \\[10pt] -{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln(1{+}y_{m/2})= -{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln\left(\frac{1}{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m}}\right) &\mbox{for $m$ even}
nodes.label: lngb1odd

nodes.name: Equation (lngb2odd,lngb2even)
nodes.statement: {\hskip -28pt\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}(r)= -{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} L\left({\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\theta_0\right)=} -{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln(1{+}y_{(m-1)/2}) = -{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} \ln\left(\frac{\sin^2\frac{(m-1)\pi}{2m}}{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m}}\right) &\mbox{for $m$ odd} \\[10pt] -{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln(1{+}x_{m/2}) = -{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} \ln\left(\frac{\sin^2\frac{m\pi}{2(m+1)}}{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m+1}}\right) &\mbox{for $m$ even}\,.
nodes.label: lngb2odd

nodes.name: Derivation of the ln g_b1, ln g_b2 plateau values
nodes.statement: Those for $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}$ and $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}$ follow from the fact that $\phi(\theta)$ and $\phi_{(x)}(\theta)$ are only significantly non-zero near to $\theta=0$. This means that the integrals (\ref{lngb1}) and (\ref{lngb2}) only receive contributions from the regions $\theta\approx 0$ and $\theta\approx \theta_0/2$, where $L(\theta)$ is, by (\ref{platx}) and (\ref{platy}), approximately constant. Pulling $L(\theta)$ out of each integral and using \begin{equation} \int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\,\phi(\theta)}= -\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\,\phi_{(\frac{1}{2})}(\theta)}=\frac{1}{2}\,,\qquad \int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\,\phi_{(\frac{3}{4})}(\theta)}=-\frac{1}{4} \end{equation} together with the plateau values given by (\ref{platx}) and (\ref{platy}) leads to (\ref{lngb1odd}) -- (\ref{lngb2even}).
nodes.statement_short: Localisation: phi and phi_(x) are concentrated at theta=0, so L can be pulled out at its plateau values and the kernel integrals evaluated.

nodes.name: Localisation of the integrals
nodes.statement: Those for $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}$ and $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}$ follow from the fact that $\phi(\theta)$ and $\phi_{(x)}(\theta)$ are only significantly non-zero near to $\theta=0$. This means that the integrals (\ref{lngb1}) and (\ref{lngb2}) only receive contributions from the regions $\theta\approx 0$ and $\theta\approx \theta_0/2$, where $L(\theta)$ is, by (\ref{platx}) and (\ref{platy}), approximately constant.
nodes.statement_short: The integrals only see theta near 0 and theta_0/2, where L is constant.

nodes.name: Evaluate kernel integrals
nodes.statement: Pulling $L(\theta)$ out of each integral and using \begin{equation} \int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\,\phi(\theta)}= -\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\,\phi_{(\frac{1}{2})}(\theta)}=\frac{1}{2}\,,\qquad \int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\,\phi_{(\frac{3}{4})}(\theta)}=-\frac{1}{4} \end{equation} together with the plateau values given by (\ref{platx}) and (\ref{platy}) leads to (\ref{lngb1odd}) -- (\ref{lngb2even}).
nodes.statement_short: Pull L out and use the integrals of phi and phi_(3/4).

nodes.name: Equation at line 786
nodes.statement: \int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\,\phi(\theta)}= -\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\,\phi_{(\frac{1}{2})}(\theta)}=\frac{1}{2}\,,\qquad \int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\,\phi_{(\frac{3}{4})}(\theta)}=-\frac{1}{4}

nodes.name: Sum ln g_0+ln g_b1+ln g_b2 = ln g(m,1,1)
nodes.statement: When $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{0}$, $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}$ and $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}$ are summed, the pieces which depend on whether $m$ is odd or even cancel, leaving the following simple result, valid for all values of $m$: \begin{equation} \ln g^{\phantom o}_{0}+\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}+\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}= \ln\left(\left(\frac{8}{m(m+1)}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}} \sqrt{\sin\frac{\pi}{m}\sin\frac{\pi}{m+1}}\right)\,. \end{equation}
conclusions: the pieces which depend on whether $m$ is odd or even cancel

nodes.name: Sum ln g_0+ln g_b1+ln g_b2
nodes.statement: \ln g^{\phantom o}_{0}+\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}+\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}= \ln\left(\left(\frac{8}{m(m+1)}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}} \sqrt{\sin\frac{\pi}{m}\sin\frac{\pi}{m+1}}\right)\,.
nodes.label: lng0sum

nodes.name: Partial sum is a Cardy boundary entropy
nodes.statement: This is the logarithm of $g(m,1,1)$ or $g(m,m{-}1,1)$, the boundary entropy of the conformal boundary condition associated with the bulk vacuum field or its ${\mathbb Z}_2$ spin flip conjugate.
conclusions: This is the logarithm of $g(m,1,1)$ or $g(m,m{-}1,1)$

nodes.name: Plateau value of ln g_b3
nodes.statement: The integral (\ref{lngb3}) receives contributions from $\theta\approx\pm\theta_{b1}$ and $\theta\approx\pm\theta_{b2}$\,; if these regions lie within the $x$- and $y$-type intervals (\ref{platx}) and (\ref{platy}) then, pulling $L(\theta)$ outside the integrals and recalling that $L(\theta)=L(-\theta)$, \begin{equation} \ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3}(r)= {\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\left(L\left(\theta_{b1}\right)+L\left(\theta_{b2}\right)\right) \end{equation} and the value of $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3}(r)$ will not change for small changes in $r$.
assumptions: if these regions lie within the $x$- and $y$-type intervals (\ref{platx}) and (\ref{platy})
conclusions: the value of $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3}(r)$ will not change for small changes in $r$

nodes.name: Equation (lngb3f)
nodes.statement: \ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3}(r)= {\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\left(L\left(\theta_{b1}\right)+L\left(\theta_{b2}\right)\right)
nodes.label: lngb3f

nodes.name: Locations of boundary transitions
nodes.statement: Conversely, $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3}(r)$ will undergo a crossover whenever $r$ is such that either $\theta_{b1}$ or $\theta_{b2}$ lies on a boundary between the intervals (\ref{platx}) and (\ref{platy}). This means that there will be boundary transitions associated with the parameter $\theta_{b1}$ at \begin{equation} \ln(r)=-k\theta_0-\theta_{b1}\,,\quad k=0,1,\dots \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \ln(r)=-k\theta_0+\theta_{b1}\,,\quad k=A,A{+}1,\dots \end{equation} where $A=\lceil 2\theta_{b1}/\theta_0\rceil$, the smallest integer greater than or equal to $2\theta_{b1}/\theta_0$\,. An analogous formula holds for $\theta_{b2}$.
nodes.statement_short: ln g_b3 has a crossover whenever theta_b1 or theta_b2 crosses an interval boundary, at ln r = -k theta_0 -/+ theta_b1.

nodes.name: Equation at line 841
nodes.statement: \ln(r)=-k\theta_0-\theta_{b1}\,,\quad k=0,1,\dots

nodes.name: Equation at line 845
nodes.statement: \ln(r)=-k\theta_0+\theta_{b1}\,,\quad k=A,A{+}1,\dots

nodes.name: The (1,1) flow for infinite boundary parameters
nodes.statement: If the limit $\theta_{b1}\to\infty$, $\theta_{b2}\to\infty$ is taken {\em before}\/ $r$ is varied, we see that there is one flow which simply moves through the $(1,1)$ boundary conditions in the successive minimal models, its $g$-function being given by $\ln g(r)=\ln g^{\phantom o}_{0}(r)+\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}(r)+\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}(r)$ for {\em all}\/ values of $r$.
assumptions: If the limit $\theta_{b1}\to\infty$, $\theta_{b2}\to\infty$ is taken {\em before}\/ $r$ is varied
conclusions: there is one flow which simply moves through the $(1,1)$ boundary conditions in the successive minimal models

nodes.name: Lower bound on g-function flows
nodes.statement: Notice that since $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3}(r)$ is manifestly positive, all other $g$-function flows must lie above this limiting curve, an off-critical generalisation of the fact that at a fixed point the lowest-possible boundary entropy is always found for the $(1,1)$ boundary condition.
conclusions: all other $g$-function flows must lie above this limiting curve

nodes.name: Possible plateau values of L(theta)
nodes.statement: From (\ref{Ls}) and the immediately-following remarks, the possible values of $L(\theta)$ on these intervals are the elements of the set \begin{equation} \left\{\ln(1+x_a), \ln(1+y_b)\right\} \end{equation} where the indices $a$ and $b$ lie in the ranges \begin{equation} a\in\{1,\cdots,m\},\;b\in\{1,\cdots,m-1\} \end{equation} and the value of $0$, found for $|\theta|\gg\ln(1/r)$, arises when $a$ is equal to $1$ or $m$, or $b$ is equal to $1$ or $m{-}1$.

nodes.name: Equation (lxy)
nodes.statement: \left\{\ln(1+x_a), \ln(1+y_b)\right\}
nodes.label: lxy

nodes.name: Equation (ab)
nodes.statement: a\in\{1,\cdots,m\},\;b\in\{1,\cdots,m-1\}
nodes.label: ab

nodes.name: Reduced index ranges
nodes.statement: The symmetries $x_{m+1-a}=x_a$, $y_{m-b}=y_b$ could have been used to restrict the indices $a$ and $b$ to \begin{eqnarray} a\in\{1,\cdots,\frac{m+1}{2}\},\;b\in\{1,\cdots,\frac{m-1}{2}\}\quad &\mbox{for m odd}&\nonumber\\ \mbox{and}\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad{a,b}\in\{1,\cdots,\frac{m}{2}\} \quad &\mbox{for m even}& \end{eqnarray} but for reasons to be explained below it will be convenient to keep with the larger ranges.

nodes.name: Equation (abr)
nodes.statement: a\in\{1,\cdots,\frac{m+1}{2}\},\;b\in\{1,\cdots,\frac{m-1}{2}\}\quad &\mbox{for m odd}&\nonumber\\ \mbox{and}\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad{a,b}\in\{1,\cdots,\frac{m}{2}\} \quad &\mbox{for m even}&
nodes.label: abr

nodes.name: Boundary-condition dictionary for g-function values
nodes.statement: We found that this value can always be expressed as a sum of Cardy $g$-function values (\ref{gmab}), according to the following rules, where we introduce the convenient notation $[x_a,y_b]$ and so on to denote the particular combinations of boundary conditions which arise: \begin{equation} \!\!\! \begin{array}{lll} L(\theta_{b1})&L(\theta_{b2})&\mbox{Boundary condition}\\[3pt] \ln\left(1{+}x_a\right)&\ln\left(1{+}y_b\right)& \rlap{$[x_a,y_b]$}\phantom{[x_p,x_q]} \equiv (b,a)\\ \ln\left(1{+}x_p\right)&\ln\left(1{+}x_q\right)& [x_p,x_q]\equiv (1,|p{-}q|{+}1)\& (1,|p{-}q|{+}3)\& \cdots\& (1,m{-}|p{+}q{-}m{-}1|)\\ \ln\left(1{+}y_r\right)&\ln\left(1{+}y_s\right)& \rlap{$[y_r,y_s]$}\phantom{[x_p,x_q]} \equiv (|r{-}s|{+}1,1)\& (|r{-}s|{+}3,1)\& \cdots\& (m{-}1{-}|r{+}s{-}m|,1)\\ \end{array} \end{equation} with the same result for $\theta_{b1}\leftrightarrow\theta_{b2}$.
conclusions: this value can always be expressed as a sum of Cardy $g$-function values (\ref{gmab})
nodes.statement_short: Each pair of plateau values (L(theta_b1),L(theta_b2)) gives a g-value equal to a sum of Cardy g-values, via the rules [x_a,y_b], [x_p,x_q], [y_r,y_s].

nodes.name: Boundary-condition dictionary [x_a,y_b]
nodes.statement: \!\!\! \begin{array}{lll} L(\theta_{b1})&L(\theta_{b2})&\mbox{Boundary condition}\\[3pt] \ln\left(1{+}x_a\right)&\ln\left(1{+}y_b\right)& \rlap{$[x_a,y_b]$}\phantom{[x_p,x_q]} \equiv (b,a)\\ \ln\left(1{+}x_p\right)&\ln\left(1{+}x_q\right)& [x_p,x_q]\equiv (1,|p{-}q|{+}1)\& (1,|p{-}q|{+}3)\& \cdots\& (1,m{-}|p{+}q{-}m{-}1|)\\ \ln\left(1{+}y_r\right)&\ln\left(1{+}y_s\right)& \rlap{$[y_r,y_s]$}\phantom{[x_p,x_q]} \equiv (|r{-}s|{+}1,1)\& (|r{-}s|{+}3,1)\& \cdots\& (m{-}1{-}|r{+}s{-}m|,1)\\ \end{array}
nodes.label: gident

nodes.name: Simplified dictionary on reduced ranges
nodes.statement: Notice that if all indices are restricted to the reduced ranges (\ref{abr}), the rules simplify to \begin{equation} \begin{array}{lll} L(\theta_{b1})&L(\theta_{b2})&\mbox{Boundary condition}\\[3pt] \ln\left(1+x_a\right)&\ln\left(1+y_b\right)&(b,a)\\ \ln\left(1+x_p\right)&\ln\left(1+x_q\right)& (1,|p{-}q|{+}1)\& (1,|p{-}q|{+}3)\& \cdots\& (1,p{+}q{-}1)\\ \ln\left(1+y_r\right)&\ln\left(1+y_s\right)& (|r{-}s|{+}1,1)\& (|r{-}s|{+}3,1)\& \cdots\& (r{+}s{-}1,1)\,. \end{array} \end{equation}
assumptions: if all indices are restricted to the reduced ranges (\ref{abr})

nodes.name: Equation (gidentr)
nodes.statement: \begin{array}{lll} L(\theta_{b1})&L(\theta_{b2})&\mbox{Boundary condition}\\[3pt] \ln\left(1+x_a\right)&\ln\left(1+y_b\right)&(b,a)\\ \ln\left(1+x_p\right)&\ln\left(1+x_q\right)& (1,|p{-}q|{+}1)\& (1,|p{-}q|{+}3)\& \cdots\& (1,p{+}q{-}1)\\ \ln\left(1+y_r\right)&\ln\left(1+y_s\right)& (|r{-}s|{+}1,1)\& (|r{-}s|{+}3,1)\& \cdots\& (r{+}s{-}1,1)\,. \end{array}
nodes.label: gidentr

nodes.name: Spin-flip symmetries of the dictionary
nodes.statement: First, ambiguity arises from the equalities $g(m,a,b)=g(m,m{-}a,b)$, $g(m,a,b)=g(m,a,m{+}1{-}b)$. These are related to the symmetries $L(\theta)=L(-\theta)$, $x_a=x_{m+1-a}$, $y_a=y_{m-a}$ of $L(\theta)$ and its plateau values, and, more precisely, to the following symmetries of the boundary condition combinations given in (\ref{gident}): \begin{align} [x_a,y_b]&= [x_{m+1-a},y_{m-b}] & \overline{[x_a,y_b]}&= [x_{m+1-a},y_{b}]= [x_{a},y_{m-b}] \nonumber\\[3pt] [x_p,x_q]&= [x_{m+1-p},x_{m+1-q}]& \overline{[x_p,x_q]}&= [x_{m+1-p},x_{q}]= [x_{p},x_{m+1-q}] \\[3pt] [y_r,y_s]&= [y_{m-r},y_{m-s}]& \overline{[y_r,y_s]}&= [y_{m-r},y_{s}]= [y_{r},y_{m-s}] \nonumber \end{align} where the overbar denotes the ${\mathbb Z}_2$ `spin flip' symmetry mentioned just after (\ref{gmab}), acting on individual Cardy boundaries as $\overline{(a,b)}=(m{-}a,b)\equiv (a,m{+}1{-}b)$\,.
nodes.statement_short: The g-value ambiguities correspond to symmetries of the bracket combinations, including the Z_2 spin flip overbar.

nodes.name: Equation (spinflip)
nodes.statement: [x_a,y_b]&= [x_{m+1-a},y_{m-b}] & \overline{[x_a,y_b]}&= [x_{m+1-a},y_{b}]= [x_{a},y_{m-b}] \nonumber\\[3pt] [x_p,x_q]&= [x_{m+1-p},x_{m+1-q}]& \overline{[x_p,x_q]}&= [x_{m+1-p},x_{q}]= [x_{p},x_{m+1-q}] \\[3pt] [y_r,y_s]&= [y_{m-r},y_{m-s}]& \overline{[y_r,y_s]}&= [y_{m-r},y_{s}]= [y_{r},y_{m-s}] \nonumber

nodes.name: Resolving the spin-flip ambiguity
nodes.statement: As remarked in~\cite{Dorey:2009vg}, it should be possible to resolve such ambiguities in a systematic fashion by studying the renormalisation group flows of the inner products of finite-volume excited states~\cite{Bazhanov:1996aq,Dorey:1996re} with the boundary states, but we shall leave this for future work.

nodes.name: Accidental degeneracies of g-values
nodes.statement: Second, there are sometimes further, more accidental, degeneracies in the set of non-negative-integer sums of Cardy $g$-function values -- for example, $g(5,1,3)=2g(5,1,1)$, so that in ${\cal M}_5$ the $(1,3)$ and $(1,1)\&(1,1)$ boundary conditions cannot be distinguished by their $g$-function values alone.

nodes.name: The dictionary (gident) is correct
nodes.statement: Nevertheless, and modulo the spin flip ambiguity just described, (\ref{gident}) is the only set of decompositions we have found which works in a uniform fashion for all $m$. From now on we shall assume that it is correct, and mostly leave the spin flip ambiguity implicit.

nodes.name: Derivation of the transition skeleton
nodes.statement: Continuing to suppose that the bulk theory is in the vicinity of the bulk fixed point ${\cal M}_m$, we now let $\ln(r)$ vary from the lower to the upper end of the range (\ref{rrange}), that is from $-(m{-}2)\theta_0/2$ to $-(m{-}3)\theta_0/2$\,. The centres of the intervals (\ref{platx}) and (\ref{platy}) remain fixed, at $\theta=z_i$, $i=1\dots 2m{-}5$, but the widths of the $x$-type intervals, $\alpha\equiv 2\ln(1/r)-(m{-}3)\theta_0$, decrease from $\theta_0$ to zero, while those of the $y$-type intervals, $\theta_0-\alpha$, increase from zero to $\theta_0$. Thus so long as $|\theta_{b1}|< (m{-}2)\theta_0/2$ and $\theta_{b1}$ is not an integer multiple of $\theta_0/2$, the regions $\theta\approx\pm\theta_{b1}$ move from $x$-type intervals to $y$-type intervals during this process, and the value of $L(\pm\theta_{b1})$, and hence that of the $g$-function, undergoes a change. For brevity we will phrase the rest of the discussion in terms of the intervals seen by $L(\theta_{b1})$, but we could equally look at $L(-\theta_{b1})$. By the ${\mathbb Z}_2$ ambiguity just discussed this might lead to different boundary conditions being assigned but since the $g$-functions are blind to their difference, we will ignore this issue for now. In fact, it will be convenient to allow $\theta_{b1}$ (and $\theta_{b2}$) to take positive and negative values, so all options are in any case covered. Suppose, then, that at the start of the process $\theta_{b1}$ is in the $x$-type interval centred at $\theta=z_{2r-3}$, and $\theta_{b2}$ is in the $x$-type interval centred at $\theta=z_{2s-3}$, corresponding to plateau values for $L(\theta_{b1})$ and $L(\theta_{b2})$ equal to $\ln(1+x_r)$ and $\ln(1+x_s)$ respectively. The $y$-type interval that $\theta_{b1}$ moves to depends on its position relative to $z_{2r-3}$. If $\theta_{b1}>z_{2r-3}$ then $L(\theta_{b1})$ moves to the plateau $\ln(1+y_{r-1})$, while if $\theta_{b1}<z_{2r-3}$ it moves to the plateau $\ln(1+y_r)$. An identical set of possibilities occurs for $L(\theta_{b2})$, with a transition which may occur before of after that in $L(\theta_{b1})$ depending on the relative distances of $\theta_{b1}$ and $\theta_{b2}$ from the centres of their original ($x$-type) intervals.
nodes.statement_short: Track which y-type interval theta_b1, theta_b2 enter as the x-type intervals shrink while ln r runs across the M_m plateau.

nodes.name: Interval widths change across the plateau
nodes.statement: Continuing to suppose that the bulk theory is in the vicinity of the bulk fixed point ${\cal M}_m$, we now let $\ln(r)$ vary from the lower to the upper end of the range (\ref{rrange}), that is from $-(m{-}2)\theta_0/2$ to $-(m{-}3)\theta_0/2$\,. The centres of the intervals (\ref{platx}) and (\ref{platy}) remain fixed, at $\theta=z_i$, $i=1\dots 2m{-}5$, but the widths of the $x$-type intervals, $\alpha\equiv 2\ln(1/r)-(m{-}3)\theta_0$, decrease from $\theta_0$ to zero, while those of the $y$-type intervals, $\theta_0-\alpha$, increase from zero to $\theta_0$. Thus so long as $|\theta_{b1}|< (m{-}2)\theta_0/2$ and $\theta_{b1}$ is not an integer multiple of $\theta_0/2$, the regions $\theta\approx\pm\theta_{b1}$ move from $x$-type intervals to $y$-type intervals during this process, and the value of $L(\pm\theta_{b1})$, and hence that of the $g$-function, undergoes a change.
nodes.statement_short: As ln r runs across the M_m range, x-type widths shrink and y-type widths grow.

nodes.name: Reduce to L(theta_b1)
nodes.statement: For brevity we will phrase the rest of the discussion in terms of the intervals seen by $L(\theta_{b1})$, but we could equally look at $L(-\theta_{b1})$. By the ${\mathbb Z}_2$ ambiguity just discussed this might lead to different boundary conditions being assigned but since the $g$-functions are blind to their difference, we will ignore this issue for now. nodes.name: Initial x-type intervals
nodes.statement: Suppose, then, that at the start of the process $\theta_{b1}$ is in the $x$-type interval centred at $\theta=z_{2r-3}$, and $\theta_{b2}$ is in the $x$-type interval centred at $\theta=z_{2s-3}$, corresponding to plateau values for $L(\theta_{b1})$ and $L(\theta_{b2})$ equal to $\ln(1+x_r)$ and $\ln(1+x_s)$ respectively.

nodes.name: Where theta_b1 moves
nodes.statement: The $y$-type interval that $\theta_{b1}$ moves to depends on its position relative to $z_{2r-3}$. If $\theta_{b1}>z_{2r-3}$ then $L(\theta_{b1})$ moves to the plateau $\ln(1+y_{r-1})$, while if $\theta_{b1}<z_{2r-3}$ it moves to the plateau $\ln(1+y_r)$.

nodes.name: Skeleton of pure-boundary transitions near M_m
nodes.statement: Putting these ingredients together gives the following `skeleton' of transitions from an initial situation where $L(\theta_{b1})=\ln(1{+}x_r)$ and $L(\theta_{b2})=\ln(1{+}x_s)$\,: \[ \begin{CD} [y_{r},y_{s}] @<<< [x_r,y_{s}] @>>> [y_{r-1},y_{s}] \\[2pt] @AAA @AAA @AAA\\[2pt] [y_{r},x_{s}] @<<< [x_r,x_{s}] @>>> [y_{r-1},x_{s}] \\[2pt] @VVV @VVV @VVV\\[2pt] [y_{r},y_{s-1}] @<<< [x_r,y_{s-1}] @>>> [y_{r-1},y_{s-1}] \end{CD} \] This diagram encapsulates the boundary flows seen while the bulk is in the vicinity of ${\cal M}_m$, if $\theta_{b1}$ and $\theta_{b2}$ are in the intervals $[z_{2r-3}-\theta_0/2,z_{2r-3}+\theta_0/2]$, $[z_{2s-3}-\theta_0/2,z_{2s-3}+\theta_0/2]$. The complete set of flows seen near to ${\cal M}_m$ is the union of a number of such diagrams, so as to cover the full ranges $|\theta_{b1}|\le (m{-}2)\theta_0/2$, $|\theta_{b2}|\le (m{-}2)\theta_0/2$.
nodes.statement_short: From [x_r,x_s] the boundary flows go to [y_r or y_{r-1}, ...] combinations, a 3x3 skeleton; the full set near M_m is a union of these.

nodes.name: Grid of boundary flows at m=5
nodes.statement: To give one example, at $m=5$ this results in a $7\times 7$ grid, the lower ($\theta_{b2}\ge 0$) half of which is: \[ \begin{array}{ccccccccccccc} \vdots &&\vdots &&\vdots &&\vdots &&\vdots &&\vdots &&\vdots \\[2pt] [y_4,x_3] &\!\!\!\xleftarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [x_4,x_3] &\!\!\!\xrightarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [y_3,x_3] &\!\!\!\xleftarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [x_3,x_3] &\!\!\!\xrightarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [y_2,x_3] &\!\!\!\xleftarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [x_2,x_3] &\!\!\!\xrightarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [y_1,x_3] \\[10pt] \Big\downarrow&& \Big\downarrow&& \Big\downarrow&& \Big\downarrow&& \Big\downarrow&& \Big\downarrow&& \Big\downarrow\\[10pt] [y_4,y_2] &\!\!\!\xleftarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [x_4,y_2] &\!\!\!\xrightarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [y_3,y_2] &\!\!\!\xleftarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [x_3,y_2] &\!\!\!\xrightarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [y_2,y_2] &\!\!\!\xleftarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [x_2,y_2] &\!\!\!\xrightarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [y_1,y_2] \\[10pt] \Big\uparrow&& \Big\uparrow&& \Big\uparrow&& \Big\uparrow&& \Big\uparrow&& \Big\uparrow&& \Big\uparrow\\[10pt] [y_4,x_2] &\!\!\!\xleftarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [x_4,x_2] &\!\!\!\xrightarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [y_3,x_2] &\!\!\!\xleftarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [x_3,x_2] &\!\!\!\xrightarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [y_2,x_2] &\!\!\!\xleftarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [x_2,x_2] &\!\!\!\xrightarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [y_1,x_2] \\[10pt] \Big\downarrow&& \Big\downarrow&& \Big\downarrow&& \Big\downarrow&& \Big\downarrow&& \Big\downarrow&& \Big\downarrow\\[10pt] [y_4,y_1] &\!\!\!\xleftarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [x_4,y_1] &\!\!\!\xrightarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [y_3,y_1] &\!\!\!\xleftarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [x_3,y_1] &\!\!\!\xrightarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [y_2,y_1] &\!\!\!\xleftarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [x_2,y_1] &\!\!\!\xrightarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [y_1,y_1] \end{array} \]

nodes.name: Symmetries of the flow diagram
nodes.statement: Notice that the figure is symmetrical about the diagonals $\theta_{b1}=\theta_{b2}$ and $\theta_{b1}=-\theta_{b2}$, while negating either $\theta_{b1}$ or $\theta_{b2}$ individually has the same effect as the ${\mathbb Z}_2$ spin flip. This second feature means that the boundary conditions in the middle column on the figure, $\theta_{b1}=0$ (or equivalently, the top row shown, $\theta_{b2}=0$) are mapped into themselves under the spin flip. As follows from (\ref{spinflip}), the corresponding properties hold for all other values of $m$, if it is assumed that the rules (\ref{gident}) are correct in general.

nodes.name: L(theta) during a bulk transition
nodes.statement: The bulk flow occurs when $\ln(r)$ varies through a region centred on $\ln(r)= -(m{-}3)\theta_0/2$ which is of size of order one as $\theta_0\to\infty$. As this happens the form of $L(\theta)$ changes: the $x$-type plateaux for ${\cal M}_m$ shrink to zero size, while the $y$-type plateau of height $\ln(1+y_a)|_{{\cal M}_m}$, $a=1\dots m{-}1$, for ${\cal M}_m$ becomes the $x$-type plateau $\ln(1+x_a)|_{{\cal M}_{m-1}}$ for ${\cal M}_{m-1}$, with $y$-type plateaux for ${\cal M}_{m-1}$ opening up between these as $\ln(r)$ increases further. (By (\ref{xy}), $\ln(1+y_a)|_{{\cal M}_m}=\ln(1+x_a)|_{{\cal M}_{m-1}}$, so there is no sudden change in heights implied by the redesignation of $y$-type to $x$-type plateaux over the transition.)
nodes.statement_short: During the M_m -> M_{m-1} bulk crossover x-type plateaux shrink and y-type plateaux of M_m become x-type plateaux of M_{m-1} with equal heights.

nodes.name: Boundary flows accompanying the bulk flow M_m -> M_{m-1}
nodes.statement:
Now consider the behaviour of the logarithm of the full $g$-function, $\ln g=\ln g^{\phantom o}_{0}+\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}+\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}+\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3}$, as ${\cal M}_m$ flows to ${\cal M}_{m-1}$. From (ef{lng0sum}), the sum of the first three terms, $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{0}+\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}+\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}$, changes from $\ln g(m,1,1)$ to $\ln g(m{-}1,1,1)$. The behaviour of the remaining piece, $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3}$, depends on the values of $	heta_{b1}$ and $	heta_{b2}$. Suppose first that both $|	heta_{b1}|\le (m{-}3)	heta_0/2$ and $|	heta_{b2}|\le (m{-}3)	heta_0/2$, so that neither boundary parameter has become decoupled at the point of the bulk transition under discussion. There are then three cases: \smallskip 
oindent { f (i)} If neither $	heta_{b1}$ nor $	heta_{b2}$ are at the centre of what had been an $x$-type plateau for ${\cal M}_m$, that is if  egin{equation} 	heta_{b1}, 	heta_{b2} 
eq (m{-}3)	heta_0/2-k	heta_0\,,\qquad k=0,1,\dots m-3 \end{equation} then both $	heta_{b1}$ and $	heta_{b2}$ will have undergone a `pure-boundary' transition of the sort described earlier, from an $x$-type onto a $y$-type plateau, {\em before}/ the ${\cal M}_m	o{\cal M}_{m-1}$ transition is reached. Thus the conformal boundary condition seen just before the bulk transition occurs will correspond to some pair $[y_r,y_s]|_{{\cal M}_m}$ where $2\le r,s\le m{-}2$, corresponding to $	heta_{b1}$ and $	heta_{b2}$ lying in the intervals $((m{-}3)	heta_0/2{-}(r{-}1)	heta_0\,,\,(m{-}3)	heta_0/2{-}(r{-}2)	heta_0)$ and $((m{-}3)	heta_0/2{-}(s{-}1)	heta_0\,,\,(m{-}3)	heta_0/2{-}(s{-}2)	heta_0)$\,. After the transition the plateau values will not have changed but their interpretations will have, to the pair $[x_r,x_s]|_{{\cal M}_{m-1}}$\,. Translated into specific conformal boundary conditions using (ef{gident}) at $m$ and $m-1$ the flow is therefore  egin{equation}  egin{array}{cl} (f,1)\,\&\, (f{+}2,1)\,\&\, \cdots\,\&\, (g,1) & ~~{\cal M}_m\[4pt] \downarrow & \[5pt] (1,f)\,\&\, (1,f{+}2)\,\&\, \cdots\,\&\, (1,g) & ~~{\cal M}_{m-1} \end{array} \end{equation} where  egin{equation} f=|r{-}s|{+}1~,\quad g=m{-}1{-}|r{+}s{-}m| \quad \mbox{and}~~ 2\le r,s \le m{-}2\,. \end{equation} Via (ef{spinflip}) and the symmetry under $	heta_{b1}\leftrightarrow	heta_{b2}$ the full set of options is explored by restricting $r$ and $s$ to the fundamental domain $2\le r\le s\le m-2$, $r+s\le m$. In fact, (ef{rsrange}) is equivalent to $f$ and $g$ in (ef{case1}) being restricted by  egin{equation} 1\le f<g\le m-1\,,\quad f-g\in 2{\mathbb Z}\,. \end{equation} Notice that these, the generic flows, always start at `sinks' on networks of pure-boundary flows such as figure ef{m=5}, and end on `sources' on the corresponding network one minimal model down. \smallskip 
oindent { f (ii)} If one of $	heta_{b1}$ or $	heta_{b2}$ lies at the centre of an $x$-type plateau for ${\cal M}_m$, then it remains on that plateau right up to the moment of the bulk transition, after which it will instead lie in the centre of a $y$-type plateau for ${\cal M}_{m-1}$. If this centre is located at $	heta=(m-3)	heta_0/2-(s{-}2)	heta_0$, $2\le s\le m{-}1$, then the corresponding value of $L(	heta)$ moves from $\ln(1{+}x_s)|_{{\cal M}_m}$ to $\ln(1{+}y_{s-1})|_{{\cal M}_{m-1}}$\,. The other plateau value simply changes its designation from $\ln(1{+}y_r)|_{{\cal M}_m}$ to $\ln(1{+}x_r)|_{{\cal M}_{m-1}}$\,, as in case~{ f (i)}. Thus the boundary condition flow is $[x_s,y_r]|_{{\cal M}_m}	o [y_{s-1},x_r]_{{\cal M}_{m-1}}$, or  egin{equation}  egin{array}{cl} (r,s) & ~~{\cal M}_m\[4pt] \downarrow & \[5pt] (s{-}1,r) & ~~{\cal M}_{m-1} \end{array} \end{equation} where  egin{equation} 2\le r\le m{-}2\,,\quad 2\le s\le m{-}1\,. \end{equation} \smallskip 
oindent { f (iii)} Lastly, if both $	heta_{b1}$ and $	heta_{b2}$ are at the centres of $x$-type plateaux for ${\cal M}_m$, say at $(m-3)	heta_0/2-(r{-}2)	heta_0$ and $(m-3)	heta_0/2-(s{-}2)	heta_0$ with $2\le r,s\le m{-}1$, then reasoning as above the boundary condition flow is $[x_r,x_s]|_{{\cal M}_m}	o [y_{r-1},y_{s-1}]|_{{\cal M}_{m-1}}$, or  egin{equation}  egin{array}{cl} (1,f)\,\&\,(1,f{+}2)\,\&\,\cdots\,\&\,(1,g) & ~~{\cal M}_{m}\[4pt] \downarrow & \[5pt] (f,1)\,\&\,(f{+}2,1)\,\&\,\cdots\,\&\,(g{-}2,1) & ~~{\cal M}_{m-1} \end{array} \end{equation} where this time  egin{equation} f=|r{-}s|{+}1~,\quad g=m{-}|r{+}s{-}m{-}1| \quad \mbox{and}~~ 2\le r,s \le m{-}1\,, \end{equation} or equivalently  egin{equation} 1\le f<g\le m\,,\quad f-g\in 2{\mathbb Z}\,. \end{equation} For these (least-generic) cases the flows are always from sources to sinks on neighbouring pairs of pure-boundary networks such as figure ef{m=5}, and decrease by one the number of superposed Cardy states.
nodes.statement_short: With both boundary parameters coupled, the bulk flow M_m -> M_{m-1} drives three kinds of boundary flow, according to how many parameters sit at x-plateau centres.

nodes.name: Case (i): generic flows
nodes.statement: {\bf (i)} If neither $\theta_{b1}$ nor $\theta_{b2}$ are at the centre of what had been an $x$-type plateau for ${\cal M}_m$, that is if \begin{equation} \theta_{b1}, \theta_{b2} \neq (m{-}3)\theta_0/2-k\theta_0\,,\qquad k=0,1,\dots m-3 \end{equation} then both $\theta_{b1}$ and $\theta_{b2}$ will have undergone a `pure-boundary' transition of the sort described earlier, from an $x$-type onto a $y$-type plateau, {\em before}\/ the ${\cal M}_m\to{\cal M}_{m-1}$ transition is reached. Thus the conformal boundary condition seen just before the bulk transition occurs will correspond to some pair $[y_r,y_s]|_{{\cal M}_m}$ where $2\le r,s\le m{-}2$, corresponding to $\theta_{b1}$ and $\theta_{b2}$ lying in the intervals $((m{-}3)\theta_0/2{-}(r{-}1)\theta_0\,,\,(m{-}3)\theta_0/2{-}(r{-}2)\theta_0)$ and $((m{-}3)\theta_0/2{-}(s{-}1)\theta_0\,,\,(m{-}3)\theta_0/2{-}(s{-}2)\theta_0)$\,. Translated into specific conformal boundary conditions using (\ref{gident}) at $m$ and $m-1$ the flow is therefore \begin{equation} \begin{array}{cl} (f,1)\,\&\, (f{+}2,1)\,\&\, \cdots\,\&\, (g,1) & ~~{\cal M}_m\\[4pt] \downarrow & \\[5pt] (1,f)\,\&\, (1,f{+}2)\,\&\, \cdots\,\&\, (1,g) & ~~{\cal M}_{m-1} \end{array} \end{equation} where \begin{equation} f=|r{-}s|{+}1~,\quad g=m{-}1{-}|r{+}s{-}m| \quad \mbox{and}~~ 2\le r,s \le m{-}2\,. \end{equation} Via (\ref{spinflip}) and the symmetry under $\theta_{b1}\leftrightarrow\theta_{b2}$ the full set of options is explored by restricting $r$ and $s$ to the fundamental domain $2\le r\le s\le m-2$, $r+s\le m$. In fact, (\ref{rsrange}) is equivalent to $f$ and $g$ in (\ref{case1}) being restricted by \begin{equation} 1\le f<g\le m-1\,,\quad f-g\in 2{\mathbb Z}\,. \end{equation} Notice that these, the generic flows, always start at `sinks' on networks of pure-boundary flows such as figure \ref{m=5}, and end on `sources' on the corresponding network one minimal model down.

nodes.name: MA+_m TBA system

nodes.statement: This leads to the following expression for $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}$\,: \begin{align} \ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}\,&= \!\!\!\sum_{n\ge 1\atop m+n~{\rm even}} \frac{1}{2n}\mbox{antiTr}\bigl(B^n\bigr)\! \int_{{\mathbb R}^n}\!\!\phi(\theta_1{-}\theta_2)\phi(\theta_2{-}\theta_3) \cdots\phi(\theta_{n-1}{-}\theta_n)\phi(\theta_n{+}\theta_1) \,d\theta_1\!\cdots d\theta_n\nonumber \\ &=\!\!\! \sum_{n\ge 1\atop m+n~{\rm even}} \frac{1}{n2^{n+2}}\,\mbox{antiTr}\left(B^n\right) \,\,=\!\! \sum_{n\ge 1\atop m+n~{\rm even}} \frac{1}{n2^{n+2}}\,\mbox{Tr}\left(B^nJ\right) \end{align} where the tridiagonal $(m-3)\times(m-3)$ matrix $B$ is equal to the limit as $\theta_0\to\infty$ of \[\left(\begin{array}{cccccccc} 0&\frac{1}{1+e^{\epsilon\left(\frac{m-4}{2}\theta_0\right)}}&0&\cdots&0&0&0\\ \frac{1}{1+e^{\epsilon\left(\frac{m-6}{2}\theta_0\right)}}&0& \frac{1}{1+e^{\epsilon\left(\frac{m-6}{2}\theta_0\right)}}&\cdots&0&0&0\\ 0&\frac{1}{1+e^{\epsilon\left(\frac{m-8}{2}\theta_0\right)}}&0& \cdots&0&0&0\\[7pt] \vdots&\vdots&\vdots&&\vdots&\vdots&\vdots\\[7pt] 0&0&0&\cdots&\frac{1}{1+e^{\epsilon\left(-\frac{m-6}{2}\theta_0\right)}}&0 &\frac{1}{1+e^{\epsilon\left(-\frac{m-6}{2}\theta_0\right)}}\\ 0&0&0&\cdots&0&\frac{1}{1+e^{\epsilon\left(-\frac{m-4}{2}\theta_0\right)}}&0 \end{array}\right) \] The explicit form of this matrix can be found using the $L(\theta)$ plateau values (\ref{Ls}) and is \[ \left(\begin{array}{ccccccc} 0&1-\frac{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m}}{\sin^2\frac{2\pi}{m}}&0&\cdots&0&0&0\\ 1-\frac{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m}}{\sin^2\frac{3\pi}{m}}&0& 1-\frac{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m}}{\sin^2\frac{3\pi}{m}}&\cdots&0&0&0\\ 0&1-\frac{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m}}{\sin^2\frac{4\pi}{m}}&0& \cdots&0&0&0\\[7pt] \vdots&\vdots&\vdots&&\vdots&\vdots&\vdots\\[7pt] 0&0&0&\cdots&1-\frac{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m}}{\sin^2\frac{(m-3)\pi}{m}} &0&1-\frac{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m}}{\sin^2\frac{(m-3)\pi}{m}}\\ 0&0&0&\cdots&0&1-\frac{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m}}{\sin^2\frac{(m-2)\pi}{m}}&0 \end{array}\right) \] or, more concisely, \begin{equation} B_{ab}=l_{ab}\,x_{a+1}/(1{+}x_{a+1}) \end{equation} where $x_a=x_a|_{{\cal M}_{m-1}}=\frac{\sin^2(\pi a/m)}{\sin^2(\pi/m)}-1$\,, and $l_{ab}$ is the incidence matrix of the $A_{m-3}$ Dynkin diagram.
nodes.statement_short: ln g_B is a series of anti-traces of powers of the constant tridiagonal matrix B_ab=l_ab x_{a+1}/(1+x_{a+1}).

nodes.name: ln g_B series
nodes.statement: \ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}\,&= \!\!\!\sum_{n\ge 1\atop m+n~{\rm even}} \frac{1}{2n}\mbox{antiTr}\bigl(B^n\bigr)\! \int_{{\mathbb R}^n}\!\!\phi(\theta_1{-}\theta_2)\phi(\theta_2{-}\theta_3) \cdots\phi(\theta_{n-1}{-}\theta_n)\phi(\theta_n{+}\theta_1) \,d\theta_1\!\cdots d\theta_n\nonumber \\ &=\!\!\! \sum_{n\ge 1\atop m+n~{\rm even}} \frac{1}{n2^{n+2}}\,\mbox{antiTr}\left(B^n\right) \,\,=\!\! \sum_{n\ge 1\atop m+n~{\rm even}} \frac{1}{n2^{n+2}}\,\mbox{Tr}\left(B^nJ\right)
nodes.label: g0b

nodes.name: Eigenvalues of B
nodes.statement: Note that $B$ is the transpose of a matrix which arises in the analysis of small fluctuations about stationary solutions of an associated Y-system \cite{Zamolodchikov:1991vx} and has eigenvalues \begin{equation} \lambda_k=2\cos\bigl(\frac{\pi k}{m}\bigr)\,,\qquad k=2,3\dots m{-}2\,. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation at line 1678
nodes.statement: \lambda_k=2\cos\bigl(\frac{\pi k}{m}\bigr)\,,\qquad k=2,3\dots m{-}2\,.

nodes.name: [B,J]=0 and J-parity of eigenvectors
nodes.statement: For later use we note that $[B,J]=0$, and furthermore that the eigenvector $\psi_k$ of $B$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda_k$ satisfies \begin{equation} J\psi_k=(-1)^k\psi_k\,. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (Jparity)
nodes.statement: J\psi_k=(-1)^k\psi_k\,.
nodes.label: Jparity

nodes.name: Closed form of ln g_B
nodes.statement: As explained in appendix A, this information is enough to evaluate (\ref{g0b}) in closed form, with the result \begin{numcases}{\ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_m} = } \displaystyle ~\ln \left(\left(\frac{4}{m}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}\! \frac{\sin\frac{(m-1)\pi}{2m}} {\sqrt{\sin\frac{\pi}{m}}}\right) &\mbox{~~for $m$ odd} \\[15pt] ~\ln \left(\left(\frac{2}{m}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}\!\! \frac{1}{\sqrt{\sin\frac{\pi}{m}}}\right) &\mbox{~~for $m$ even} . \end{numcases}
nodes.statement_short: ln g_B for MA+_m evaluates in closed form to a log of a ratio of sines, separately for m odd and m even.

nodes.name: Closed form of ln g_B
nodes.statement: {\ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_m} = } \displaystyle ~\ln \left(\left(\frac{4}{m}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}\! \frac{\sin\frac{(m-1)\pi}{2m}} {\sqrt{\sin\frac{\pi}{m}}}\right) &\mbox{~~for $m$ odd} \\[15pt] ~\ln \left(\left(\frac{2}{m}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}\!\! \frac{1}{\sqrt{\sin\frac{\pi}{m}}}\right) &\mbox{~~for $m$ even} .
nodes.label: g0bodd

nodes.name: Derivation of the ln g_0 plateau values
nodes.statement: A missing piece of the staircase discussion from the previous section can now be filled in, namely the formulae (\ref{lng0fodd}) and (\ref{lng0feven}) for the value of $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{0}|_{{\cal M}_m}$ when the bulk staircase theory is in the vicinity of ${\cal M}_m$. In terms of the limiting $g$-function equations for ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$, this number is equal to the UV limit of $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{A}(\hat{r}) + \ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}$ as $\hat{r}\to 0$. Considering the limiting forms of the matrix $A(\theta)$, given by (\ref{Ai}), as $\hat r\to 0$, it is straightforwardly seen that \begin{equation} \ln g^{\phantom o}_{A}(0)|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_m}=\ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m+1}} \end{equation} and so \begin{equation} \ln g^{\phantom o}_{0}|_{{\cal M}_m} = \ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m+1}} + \ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_m} \end{equation} \nobreak which, via (\ref{g0bodd}) and (\ref{g0beven}), leads immediately to (\ref{lng0fodd}) and (\ref{lng0feven}).
nodes.statement_short: ln g_0 on the M_m plateau is the UV limit of ln g_A+ln g_B; the UV ln g_A equals ln g_B at m+1, so ln g_0 is a sum of two closed-form ln g_B.

nodes.name: Reduce to the UV limit
nodes.statement: A missing piece of the staircase discussion from the previous section can now be filled in, namely the formulae (\ref{lng0fodd}) and (\ref{lng0feven}) for the value of $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{0}|_{{\cal M}_m}$ when the bulk staircase theory is in the vicinity of ${\cal M}_m$. In terms of the limiting $g$-function equations for ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$, this number is equal to the UV limit of $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{A}(\hat{r}) + \ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}$ as $\hat{r}\to 0$.
nodes.statement_short: ln g_0 on the M_m plateau equals the UV limit of ln g_A+ln g_B.

nodes.name: UV ln g_A equals ln g_B at m+1
nodes.statement: Considering the limiting forms of the matrix $A(\theta)$, given by (\ref{Ai}), as $\hat r\to 0$, it is straightforwardly seen that \begin{equation} \ln g^{\phantom o}_{A}(0)|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_m}=\ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m+1}} \end{equation} and so \begin{equation} \ln g^{\phantom o}_{0}|_{{\cal M}_m} = \ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m+1}} + \ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_m} \end{equation} \nobreak which, via (\ref{g0bodd}) and (\ref{g0beven}), leads immediately to (\ref{lng0fodd}) and (\ref{lng0feven}).
nodes.statement_short: In the UV ln g_A becomes ln g_B for MA+_{m+1}; adding the two closed forms gives the result.

nodes.name: Equation (gUV)
nodes.statement: \ln g^{\phantom o}_{A}(0)|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_m}=\ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m+1}}
nodes.label: gUV

nodes.name: Equation at line 1721
nodes.statement: \ln g^{\phantom o}_{0}|_{{\cal M}_m} = \ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m+1}} + \ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_m}

nodes.name: ln g_b1 in the MA+_m limit
nodes.statement: The presence of $\phi(\theta)$ and $\delta(\theta)$ in the expression (\ref{lngb1}) for $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}$ means that this term is determined by the staircase pseudoenergy close to $\theta=0$. When $m$ is odd this remains nontrivial as the double-scaling limit is taken and, using the pseudoenergies defined in (\ref{epsadef}), $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}$ becomes \begin{equation} \ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1} = -{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\left(\phi(\theta)+ {\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\delta(\theta)\right)\!\ln(1+e^{-\epsilon_{\frac{m-1}{2}}(\theta)})}\,, \end{equation} which has UV and IR limits given by (\ref{lngb1odd}) at ${\cal M}_m$ and (\ref{lngb1even}) at ${\cal M}_{m-1}$ respectively. When $m$ is even, the staircase pseudoenergy instead becomes constant near to $\theta=0$, giving \begin{equation} \ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}=-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln(1+y_{m/2}|^{\phantom o}_{{\cal M}_{m}}) \end{equation} matching (\ref{lngb1even}) at ${\cal M}_m$ and also (\ref{lngb1odd}) at ${\cal M}_{m-1}$.
nodes.statement_short: In the limit ln g_b1 is an integral over epsilon_{(m-1)/2} for m odd, and the constant -ln(1+y_{m/2})/2 for m even.

nodes.name: Equation at line 1744
nodes.statement: \ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1} = -{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\left(\phi(\theta)+ {\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\delta(\theta)\right)\!\ln(1+e^{-\epsilon_{\frac{m-1}{2}}(\theta)})}\,,

nodes.name: Equation at line 1753
nodes.statement: \ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}=-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln(1+y_{m/2}|^{\phantom o}_{{\cal M}_{m}})

nodes.name: ln g_b2 in the MA+_m limit
nodes.statement: In contrast, the formula (\ref{lngb2}) for $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}$ involves $\phi_{(\frac{3}{4})}(\theta\pm{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\theta_0)$ and $\phi(2\theta\pm\theta_0)$, meaning that $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}$ is determined by the behaviour of $L(\theta)$ close to $\theta=\pm\theta_0/2$. For $m$ odd, the limiting form of $L(\theta\approx\pm\theta_0/2)$ is constant, and \begin{equation} \ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}=-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln(1+y_{\frac{m-1}{2}}|_{{\cal M}_{m}}) \end{equation} as in (\ref{lngb2odd}) at ${\cal M}_m$ and (\ref{lngb2even}) at ${\cal M}_{m-1}$. When $m$ is even, $L(\theta\approx\pm\theta_0/2)$ remains nontrivial and in the limit \begin{equation} \ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}=\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\bigl(\phi_{(\frac{3}{4})}(\theta) - \phi(2\theta)\bigr)\!\ln(1+e^{-\epsilon_{\frac{m-2}{2}}(\theta)})}\,, \end{equation} with UV and IR limits given by (\ref{lngb2even}) at ${\cal M}_m$ and (\ref{lngb2odd}) at ${\cal M}_{m-1}$ respectively.
nodes.statement_short: In the limit ln g_b2 is constant for m odd and an integral over epsilon_{(m-2)/2} for m even.

nodes.name: Equation at line 1767
nodes.statement: \ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}=-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln(1+y_{\frac{m-1}{2}}|_{{\cal M}_{m}})

nodes.name: Equation at line 1773
nodes.statement: \ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}=\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\bigl(\phi_{(\frac{3}{4})}(\theta) - \phi(2\theta)\bigr)\!\ln(1+e^{-\epsilon_{\frac{m-2}{2}}(\theta)})}\,,

nodes.name: ln g_b3 in the MA+_m limit
nodes.statement: To allow the last part of $\ln g^{\phantom o}_b$, $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3}$, to retain a non-trivial $\hat r$-dependence in the limit, we pick two integers $a_1$ and $a_2$ with $0\le a_i\le m{-}1$, write the boundary parameters $\theta_{b1}$ and $\theta_{b2}$ as \begin{equation} \theta_{b_i}={\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}(m{-}1{-}2a_i)\theta_0 +\hat\theta_{b_i} \end{equation} for $i=1,2$, and then take the $\theta_0\to\infty$ limit keeping $\hat\theta_{b1}$ and $\hat\theta_{b2}$ finite. Given the specification (\ref{epsadef}) of the effective pseudoenergies $\epsilon_a(\theta)$, for $1\le a_i\le m{-}2$ the staircase expression (\ref{lngb3}) for $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3}$ then reduces to \begin{align} \ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3\,\,a_1a_2}(\hat r,\hat\theta_{b1},\hat\theta_{b2}) &= {\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\sum_{i=1}^2\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\bigl(\phi(\theta-\hat\theta_{b_i})+ \phi(\theta+\hat\theta_{b_i}) \bigr)\!\ln(1+e^{-\epsilon_{a_i}(\theta)})} \nonumber\\ &= \sum_{i=1}^2\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\,\phi(\theta-\hat\theta_{b_i}) \ln(1+e^{-\epsilon_{a_i}(\theta)})} \end{align} where the symmetry $\epsilon_a(\theta)=\epsilon_{m-1-a}(-\theta)$ of the ground-state pseudoenergies for ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$ was used in going from the first line to the second. If either $a_i$ is equal to $0$ or $m{-}1$, then the staircase pseudoenergy diverges in the region of $\theta_{b_i}$, and the corresponding term in (\ref{gbiii}) is zero in the ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$ limit.
nodes.statement_short: Shifting theta_bi by (m-1-2a_i)theta_0/2, ln g_b3 reduces to integrals of phi(theta-theta_hat_bi) against L_{a_i}.

nodes.name: Equation at line 1786
nodes.statement: \theta_{b_i}={\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}(m{-}1{-}2a_i)\theta_0 +\hat\theta_{b_i}

nodes.name: ln g_b3 a1a2 in the limit
nodes.statement: \ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3\,\,a_1a_2}(\hat r,\hat\theta_{b1},\hat\theta_{b2}) &= {\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\sum_{i=1}^2\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\bigl(\phi(\theta-\hat\theta_{b_i})+ \phi(\theta+\hat\theta_{b_i}) \bigr)\!\ln(1+e^{-\epsilon_{a_i}(\theta)})} \nonumber\\ &= \sum_{i=1}^2\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\,\phi(\theta-\hat\theta_{b_i}) \ln(1+e^{-\epsilon_{a_i}(\theta)})}
nodes.label: gbiii

nodes.name: Exact g-functions for MA+_m
nodes.statement: To summarize the results of this section, our final expressions for the two-parameter families of exact $g$-functions for ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$, indexed by a pair of integers $a_1$ and $a_2$ and expressed in terms of the rescaled variables $\hat r$, $\hat\theta_{b1}$ and $\hat\theta_{b2}$, are as follows: \vskip -25pt \begin{align} \intertext{ $\bullet$ $m$ odd:} \ln g_{a_1a_2}(\hat{r},\hat\theta_{b1},\hat\theta_{b2}) &= \ln\!\left(\left(\frac{4}{m}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}\!\!\! \sqrt{\sin\frac{\pi}{m}}\right)-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\left(\phi(\theta)+ {\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\delta(\theta)\right)\!\ln(1+e^{-\epsilon_{\frac{m-1}{2}}(\theta)})} \nonumber\\[5pt] &\quad\qquad +\ln g^{\phantom o}_{A}(\hat{r}) +\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3\,\,a_1a_2}(\hat r,\hat\theta_{b1},\hat\theta_{b2})\,; \\ \intertext{ $\bullet$ $m$ even:} \ln g_{a_1a_2}(\hat{r},\hat\theta_{b1},\hat\theta_{b2}) &= \ln\!\left(\left(\frac{2}{m}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}\!\!\! \sqrt{\sin\frac{\pi}{m}}\right)+\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\Bigl(\phi_{(\frac{3}{4})}(\theta) - \phi(2\theta)\Bigr)\ln(1+e^{-\epsilon_{\frac{m-2}{2}}(\theta)})} \nonumber\\[5pt] &\quad\qquad +\ln g^{\phantom o}_{A}(\hat{r}) +\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3\,\,a_1a_2}(\hat r,\hat\theta_{b1},\hat\theta_{b2})\,. \end{align} In both cases $g^{\phantom o}_{A}$ is given by (\ref{goA}), the sum over $n$ running through even integers for $m$ odd, and odd integers for $m$ even, with the pseudoenergies involved solving the bulk ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$ TBA system (\ref{bulkmasslessTBA}). The term $g^{\phantom o}_{b3\,\,a_1a_2}$ is as defined in (\ref{gbiii}).
nodes.statement_short: Two-parameter families of exact g-functions for MA+_m, indexed by a_1,a_2: a constant, one ln g_b1 or ln g_b2 integral, ln g_A and ln g_b3.

nodes.name: Exact g-function for MA+_m, m odd
nodes.statement: \ln g_{a_1a_2}(\hat{r},\hat\theta_{b1},\hat\theta_{b2}) &= \ln\!\left(\left(\frac{4}{m}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}\!\!\! \sqrt{\sin\frac{\pi}{m}}\right)-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\left(\phi(\theta)+ {\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\delta(\theta)\right)\!\ln(1+e^{-\epsilon_{\frac{m-1}{2}}(\theta)})} \nonumber\\[5pt] &\quad\qquad +\ln g^{\phantom o}_{A}(\hat{r}) +\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3\,\,a_1a_2}(\hat r,\hat\theta_{b1},\hat\theta_{b2})\,;
nodes.label: gmodd

nodes.name: Exact g-function for MA+_m, m even
nodes.statement: \ln g_{a_1a_2}(\hat{r},\hat\theta_{b1},\hat\theta_{b2}) &= \ln\!\left(\left(\frac{2}{m}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}\!\!\! \sqrt{\sin\frac{\pi}{m}}\right)+\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\Bigl(\phi_{(\frac{3}{4})}(\theta) - \phi(2\theta)\Bigr)\ln(1+e^{-\epsilon_{\frac{m-2}{2}}(\theta)})} \nonumber\\[5pt] &\quad\qquad +\ln g^{\phantom o}_{A}(\hat{r}) +\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3\,\,a_1a_2}(\hat r,\hat\theta_{b1},\hat\theta_{b2})\,.
nodes.label: gmeven

nodes.name: Assembly of the constant terms
nodes.statement: The constant terms result from adding $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}$, given by (\ref{g0bodd}) or (\ref{g0beven}), to $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}$ for $m$ odd, and to $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}$ for $m$ even.
nodes.statement_short: Combine ln g_B with ln g_b2 (m odd) or ln g_b1 (m even) to get the constants.

nodes.name: Limiting one- and zero-parameter families
nodes.statement: Formally setting one or both of $a_1$ and $a_2$ equal to $0$ or $m{-}1$, as discussed after (\ref{gbiii}), incorporates the limiting one- and zero- parameter families of flows found by deleting the $\hat\theta_{b1}$ and/or $\hat\theta_{b2}$ dependent parts of $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3}$.

nodes.name: Zero-parameter flow g(m,1,1) -> g(m-1,1,1)
nodes.statement: If both are deleted so that $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3}$ is identically zero, then by the results of the last section the $g$-function flow should be from $g(m,1,1)$ at $\hat r=0$ to $g(m{-}1,1,1)$ as $\hat r\to\infty$.
assumptions: If both are deleted so that $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3}$ is identically zero
conclusions: the $g$-function flow should be from $g(m,1,1)$ at $\hat r=0$ to $g(m{-}1,1,1)$ as $\hat r\to\infty$

nodes.name: Check of the UV and IR limits
nodes.statement: This can be checked directly. Simplest is the UV limit. For $m$ odd, using (\ref{lngb1odd}) and (\ref{gUV}), the first three terms on the RHS of (\ref{gmodd}) tend to \begin{equation} \ln\left(\left(\frac{4}{m}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}} \!\!\sqrt{\sin{\frac{\pi}{m}}}\right) -{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln\left(\frac{1}{\sin^2\left(\frac{\pi}{m+1}\right)}\right) +\ln\left(\left(\frac{2}{m+1}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{\sin{\frac{\pi}{m+1}}}}\right) \end{equation} which is equal to $g(m,1,1)$\,. Similarly, for $m$ even, (\ref{lngb2even}) and (\ref{gUV}) imply that the first three terms on the RHS of (\ref{gmeven}) become \begin{equation} \ln\left(\left(\frac{2}{m}\right)^{\!\frac{1}{4}}\!\! \sqrt{\sin{\frac{\pi}{m}}}\right) - {\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln\left(\frac{\sin^2\left(\frac{\pi m}{2(m+1)}\right)} {\sin^2\left(\frac{\pi}{m+1}\right)}\right) + \ln\left(\left(\frac{4}{m{+}1}\right)^{\!\frac{1}{4}} \frac{\,\sin\left(\frac{m\pi}{2(m+1)}\right)} {\sqrt{\sin{\frac{\pi}{m+1}}}}\right) \end{equation} \nobreak and the value of $g(m,1,1)$ is again reproduced. \goodbreak In the $\hat r\to\infty$, IR, limit the matrix $A(\theta_i)$ defined in (\ref{Ai}) again becomes independent of $\theta$ in the central region $\theta\approx 0$ where the integrals in (\ref{goA}) have their support, and tends to the following $(m{-}2)\times (m{-}2)$ matrix: \begin{equation} A_{\rm IR}= \left(\begin{array}{cccccccc} 0&0&0&\cdots&0&0&0\\ 1-\frac{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m-1}}{\sin^2\frac{2\pi}{m-1}}&0 &1-\frac{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m-1}}{\sin^2\frac{2\pi}{m-1}}&\cdots&0&0&0\\ 0&1-\frac{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m-1}}{\sin^2\frac{3\pi}{m-1}} &0&\cdots&0&0&0\\ &&&&&&\\ \vdots&\vdots&\vdots&&\vdots&\vdots&\vdots\\ &&&&&&\\ 0&0&0&\cdots&1-\frac{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m-1}}{\sin^2\frac{(m-3)\pi}{m-1}} &0&1-\frac{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m-1}}{\sin^2\frac{(m-3)\pi}{m-1}}\\ 0&0&0&\,\cdots\,&0&~~0~~&0 \end{array}\right).\end{equation} In terms of $A_{\rm IR}$\,, \begin{equation} \ln g^{\phantom o}_{A}(\infty)=\sum_{n\ge 1\atop m+n~{\rm odd}} \frac{1}{n2^{n+2}}\,\mbox{Tr}\left((A_{\rm IR})^nJ\right). \end{equation} To evaluate this sum, observe that the central $(m{-}4)\times(m{-}4)$ sub-matrix of $A_{\rm IR}$ is the matrix $B$ for ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m-1}$. Furthermore, the zero values of all entries in the first and final rows means that the central $(m{-}4)\times(m{-}4)$ sub-matrix of $(A_{\rm IR})^n$ is just $(B|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m-1}})^n$\,, and the entries on the first and final rows are again zero. Hence the traces and antitraces of $(A_{\rm IR})^n$ are equal to those of $(B|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m-1}})^n$\,, and \begin{equation} \ln g_{0_A}(\infty)|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m}}=\ln g_{0_B}|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m-1}} \end{equation} allowing (\ref{g0bodd}) and (\ref{g0beven}) at $m{-}1$ to be used to compute $\ln g_{0_A}(\infty)|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m}}$\,. For $m$ odd, using (\ref{lngb1even}) and (\ref{g0beven}) at $m{-}1$, the first three terms of (\ref{gmodd}) therefore become \begin{equation} \ln\left(\left(\frac{4}{m}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}\!\! \sqrt{\sin{\frac{\pi}{m}}}\right) -{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln\left(\frac{1}{\sin^2\left(\frac{\pi}{m-1}\right)}\right) + \ln\left(\left(\frac{2}{m-1}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}\!\! \frac{1}{\sqrt{\sin{\frac{\pi}{m-1}}}}\right) \nonumber\\ \end{equation} which is indeed equal to $g(m{-}1,1,1)$. Similarly, for $m$ even, in the $\hat r\to\infty$ limit the first three terms of (\ref{gmeven}) are, by (\ref{lngb2odd}) and (\ref{g0bodd}) at $m{-}1$, \begin{equation} \ln\left(\left(\frac{2}{m}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}\!\! \sqrt{\sin{\frac{\pi}{m}}}\right) -{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln\left(\frac{\sin^2\left(\frac{(m-2)\pi}{2(m-1)} \right)}{\sin^2\left(\frac{\pi}{m-1}\right)}\right) +\ln\left(\left(\frac{4}{m-1}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}} \frac{\sin\left(\frac{(m-2)\pi}{2(m-1)}\right)} {\sqrt{\sin{\frac{\pi}{m-1}}}}\right) \end{equation} which again matches $g(m{-}1,1,1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Evaluate the constant terms in the UV via (gUV) and in the IR via A_IR, whose central block is B at m-1; both reproduce g(m,1,1) and g(m-1,1,1).

Furthermore, the zero values of all entries in the first and final rows means that the central $(m{-}4)\times(m{-}4)$ sub-matrix of $(A_{\rm IR})^n$ is just $(B|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m-1}})^n$\,, and the entries on the first and final rows are again zero. Hence the traces and antitraces of $(A_{\rm IR})^n$ are equal to those of $(B|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m-1}})^n$\,, and \begin{equation} \ln g_{0_A}(\infty)|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m}}=\ln g_{0_B}|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m-1}} \end{equation} allowing (\ref{g0bodd}) and (\ref{g0beven}) at $m{-}1$ to be used to compute $\ln g_{0_A}(\infty)|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m}}$\,.
