nodes.name: Cube of MA+_m flows
nodes.statement: More generally, the full equations (\ref{gmodd}) or (\ref{gmeven}) predict a collection of two-parameter families of flows, indexed by the two integers $a_1$ and $a_2$. The relevant calculations have been carried out in the last section and we won't repeat them here. Instead, in figure \ref{cubef} below we show a typical family of flows, where $r=a_1+1$ and $s=a_2+1$. All flows for $\hat\theta_{b1}$ and $\hat\theta_{b2}$ finite start in the far UV at the $[x_r,x_s]$ boundary of ${\cal M}_m$, a superposition of Cardy boundaries given by the rule (\ref{gident}). If both $\hat\theta_{b1}$ and $\hat\theta_{b2}$ are zero, the flow is directly downwards to the $[y_{r-1},y_{s-1}]$ boundary of ${\cal M}_{m-1}$, driven by the bulk perturbation. Nonzero values of $\hat\theta_{b1}$ and $\hat\theta_{b2}$ correspond to the addition of boundary perturbations to the bulk perturbation, and cause the trajectory to visit other boundaries on its way from UV to IR, as can be read from the figure.
nodes.statement_short: The a_1,a_2 families flow from [x_r,x_s] of M_m to [y_{r-1},y_{s-1}] of M_{m-1}, visiting other boundaries for nonzero boundary parameters.

nodes.name: Truncation of the cube
nodes.statement: If either of $a_1$ or $a_2$ is equal to $1$ or $m{-}2$, so that one or both of $r$ and $s$ is equal to $2$ or $m{-}1$, the cube shown in figure \ref{cubef} truncates, the equalities $x_1=y_1$ or $x_{m-1}=y_{m-2}$ within ${\cal M}_{m-1}$ causing one or two rows on the bottom face of the cube to fuse together, resulting in the flow patterns illustrated in figure \ref{cubetrunc}.

nodes.name: Generality of abelianisation
nodes.statement: Finally, it is noteworthy how the embedding of non-diagonal bulk and boundary scattering theories within higher-dimensional manifolds of integrability achieved by the staircase and HSG models manages to `abelianise' their TBA descriptions. It would be very interesting to know how general this phenomenon is, and to understand it at a deeper level.

nodes.name: Proof of the closed form of ln g_B (Appendix A)
nodes.statement:
To derive (ef{g0bodd}) and (ef{g0beven}) from (ef{g0b}), we first convert the final sum, over traces of products of powers of $B$ with $J$, into a sum of traces of pure powers of related matrices, after which the identity  egin{equation} \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} rac{1}{n}\mbox{Tr}\,M^n = -\mbox{Tr}\ln(I-M) = -\ln\mbox{Det}(I-M) \end{equation} will allow the sum to be evaluated in terms of the eigenvalues of these related matrices. There are two cases. \medskip 
oindent $ ullet$ If $m$ is odd, then the sum in (ef{g0b}) is over odd powers of $B$. Shuffling indices and using the symmetries of $B$ it can be checked that $B^nJ=(BJ)^n$ for all odd $n$, and so  egin{eqnarray} \ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}&=&  rac{1}{4} \mbox{Tr} \sum_{n\ge 1\atop n {m odd}}  rac{1}{n}\left({	extstyle rac{1}{2}} BJight)^n
onumber\ &=& rac{1}{8} \ln rac{\mbox{Det}\left(1+{	extstyle rac{1}{2}} BJight)}{\mbox{Det}\left(1-{	extstyle rac{1}{2}} BJight)}\,. \end{eqnarray} From (ef{Jparity}), the eigenvalues of $BJ$ are $(-1)^k\lambda_k$, which for $m$ odd are the numbers $2\cos(2\pi/m)$, $2\cos(4\pi/m)$\,\dots $2\cos((m{-}3)\pi/m)$, all with multiplicity two. Hence  egin{equation}  rac{\mbox{Det}\left(1+{	extstyle rac{1}{2}} BJight)}{\mbox{Det}\left(1-{	extstyle rac{1}{2}} BJight)}=  rac{\cos^4 rac{\pi}{m}\cos^4 rac{2\pi}{m}\cdots\cos^4 rac{(m-3)\pi}{2m}} {\sin^4 rac{\pi}{m}\sin^4 rac{2\pi}{m}\cdots\sin^4 rac{(m-3)\pi}{2m}}\,. \end{equation} To evaluate this we call upon some well-known trigonometric identities. For the numerator we use  egin{equation} \cos rac{\pi}{n}\cos rac{2\pi}{n}\cdots\cos rac{(n-1)\pi}{2n}=  rac{1}{2^{(n-1)/2}}\quad\mbox{for $n$ odd} \end{equation} and for the denominator  egin{equation} \sin rac{\pi}{n}\sin rac{2\pi}{n}\cdots\sin rac{(n-1)\pi}{n}=  rac{n}{2^{n-1}} \end{equation} which implies  egin{equation}\sin^2 rac{\pi}{n}\sin^2 rac{2\pi}{n}\cdots\sin^2 rac{(n-1)\pi}{2n} = rac{n}{2^{n-1}}\quad\mbox{for $n$ odd.} \end{equation} Using (ef{trig0}) and (ef{trig2}),  egin{equation}  rac{\mbox{Det}\left(1+{	extstyle rac{1}{2}} BJight)} {\mbox{Det}\left(1-{	extstyle rac{1}{2}} BJight)}=  rac{1}{m^2} rac{\sin^4 rac{(m-1)\pi}{2m}}{\cos^4 rac{(m-1)\pi}{2m}} =\left( rac{4}{m} rac{\sin^4 rac{(m-1)\pi}{2m}} {\sin^2 rac{\pi}{m}}ight)^2 \end{equation} and so (ef{lnodd}) is in agreement with (ef{g0bodd}). \medskip 
oindent $ ullet$ If $m$ is even, then the sum in (ef{g0b}) is instead over even powers of $B$. This time we make use of the identity, valid for $m$ even, that  egin{equation} \mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)=\mbox{Tr}(B^n-B^{\prime n}) \end{equation} where $B^{\prime}$ is the $(m-3)	imes(m-3)$ matrix which only differs from $B$ in the following elements:  egin{equation} B^{\prime}_{ rac{m-2}{2}, rac{m-4}{2}}= B^{\prime}_{ rac{m-2}{2}, rac{m}{2}}=0. \end{equation} To prove this identity we write the LHS as  egin{equation} \mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)= B_{i_1i_2}B_{i_2i_3}\cdots B_{i_{n-1}i_{n}}B_{i_{n}m-i_1-2} \end{equation} and note the following properties of $B$:  egin{eqnarray} B_{i,i-1}&=&B_{i,i+1}, \mbox{\quad all other entries $0$;} \ B_{ij}&=&B_{m-2-i,m-2-j}\,.  \end{eqnarray} The first of these means that (ef{Banti}) can be interpreted as a weighted sum over all $n$-step paths on the $A_{m-3}$ Dynkin diagram which start and finish at pairs of conjugate nodes $i_1$ and $m{-}2{-}i_1$, $i_1=1\dots m{-}3$, and move by one link at each step. Likewise $\mbox{Tr}(B^n)$ and $\mbox{Tr}(B'^n)$ are weighted sums over $n$-step paths on the same Dynkin diagram, but which this time start and finish at the same node $i_1$, where again $i_1$ is summed from $1$ to $m{-}3$. These observations imply that both sides of (ef{Banti}) are zero for $n$ odd, and so from now on we can take $n$ to be even (which is the case of direct interest in the current context). Due again to (ef{B0}), a term in $\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)$ with $i_1< rac{m-2}{2}$ must include the element $B_{ rac{m-2}{2} rac{m}{2}}$, and a term with $i_1> rac{m-2}{2}$ must include the element $B_{ rac{m-2}{2} rac{m-4}{2}}$. Assume first that $i_1< rac{m-2}{2}$, and consider  egin{equation} B_{i_1i_2}B_{i_2i_3}\cdots B_{i_{n-1}i_{n}}B_{i_{n},m-2-i_1} \end{equation} for some particular $i_2\dots i_n$. Suppose $B_{ rac{m-2}{2} rac{m}{2}}$ appears for the final time at $B_{i_pi_{p+1}}$, which means that $B_{i_{p+1}i_{p+2}}=B_{ rac{m}{2} rac{m+2}{2}}$. By (ef{B1}), the value of (ef{Bterm}) is unchanged if all indices $i_q$ with $q>p$ are replaced by their conjugates $m-2-i_q$. The resulting term appears in the trace not of $B^nJ$, but of $B^n$. Similarly, every term in the expansion of $\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)$ with $i_1> rac{m-2}{2}$ can be equated with a term in the expansion of $\mbox{Tr}(B^n)$ with $i_1> rac{m-2}{2}$\,. Finally, the terms in the expansions of $\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)$ and $\mbox{Tr}(B^n)$ with $i_1= rac{m-2}{2}$ are already equal, since $i_1$ is then equal to $m-2-i_1$. Thus $\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)$ is equal to the sum of the terms in the trace of $B^n$ that include either $B_{ rac{m-2}{2} rac{m}{2}}$ or $B_{ rac{m-2}{2} rac{m-4}{2}}$ at least once. Now the trace of $B'^n$ as defined by (ef{BPdef}) is equal to the trace of $B^n$ minus the terms where $B_{ rac{m-2}{2} rac{m}{2}}$ or $B_{ rac{m-2}{2} rac{m-4}{2}}$ appears at least once. Hence $\mbox{Tr}(B^n-B^{\prime n})$ gives the required terms and (ef{traceident}) holds. If $m$ is even we therefore have  egin{eqnarray} \ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}&=& \sum_{n>1\atop n~{m even}}  rac{1}{n2^{n+2}}\mbox{Tr}\,(B^nJ)
onumber \ &=& rac{1}{4} \sum_{n>1\atop n~{m even}}  rac{1}{n}\mbox{Tr}\left(\left({	extstyle rac{1}{2}} Bight)^n-\left({	extstyle rac{1}{2}} B^{\prime}ight)^night)
onumber\ &=& rac{1}{8}\ln  rac{\mbox{Det}\left(I- rac{1}{4}(B^{\prime})^2ight)} {\mbox{Det}\left(I- rac{1}{4}B^2ight)} \end{eqnarray} using (ef{lntr}). To find the eigenvalues of $B'$, $\mbox{Det}(B'-\lambda I)$ can be expanded about the middle row to see that the characteristic polynomial of $B'$ is proportional to $\lambda$ times the product of the (equal) characteristic polynomials of the upper-left and lower-right $(m{-}4)/2	imes (m{-}4)/2$ submatrices of $B'$, which we denote $B'_1$ and $B'_2$. These submatrices can be fully diagonalised using the $(m{-}4)/2$ eigenvectors $\psi_k$ of $B$ with $k$ odd: from (ef{Jparity}), these eigenvectors satisfy $J\psi_k=-\psi_k$. Hence their middle components are zero, while the neighbouring two are the negatives of each other. Given the definition (ef{BPdef}) of $B'$ this means that projecting each $\psi_k$ for $k$ odd onto its first $(m{-}4)/2$ components yields $(m{-}4)/2$ independent eigenvectors of $B'_1$ with eigenvalues $\lambda_k$, and likewise for $B'_2$. Hence the eigenvalues of $B'$ are  egin{equation} \lambda_k=2\cos igl( rac{\pi k}{m} igr)\,,\qquad k=3,5\dots m{-}3\,, \end{equation} each with multiplicity $2$, together with $0$. If $m=2$ mod $4$, then $0$ is also in the set (ef{elist}), and so the algebraic multiplicity of the zero eigenvalue is $3$, even though its geometric multiplicity turns out to be only $2$. However, this lack of full diagonalisability makes no difference to the computations of traces. We can now calculate $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}$. Evaluating (ef{lneven}) using the eigenvalues just obtained,  egin{eqnarray}  rac{\mbox{Det}\left(I- rac{1}{4}(B^{\prime})^2ight)} {\mbox{Det}\left(I- rac{1}{4}B^2ight)}&=&  rac{\sin^4 rac{3\pi}{m}\sin^4 rac{5\pi}{m}\cdots \sin^4 rac{(m-3)\pi}{m}}{\sin^2 rac{2\pi}{m}\sin^2  rac{3\pi}{m}\cdots\sin^2 rac{(m-2)\pi}{m}}
onumber\ &=& rac{\sin^2 rac{3\pi}{m}\sin^2 rac{5\pi}{m}\cdots \sin^2 rac{(m-3)\pi}{m}}{\sin^2 rac{2\pi}{m}\sin^2  rac{4\pi}{m}\cdots\sin^2 rac{(m-2)\pi}{m}}\,. \end{eqnarray} Labelling the final numerator $X$ and the denominator $Y$, (ef{trig}) at $n=m$ and $n=m/2$ respectively implies that  egin{equation} XY= rac{1}{\sin^4 rac{\pi}{m}}\left( rac{m}{2^{m-1}}ight)^2~,\qquad Y= rac{m^2}{2^{m}}\,. \end{equation} Hence  egin{equation}  rac{X}{Y}= rac{\mbox{Det}\left(I- rac{1}{4}(B^{\prime})^2ight)} {\mbox{Det}\left(I- rac{1}{4}B^2ight)}= \left( rac{2}{m\sin^2 rac{\pi}{m}}ight)^2 \end{equation} 
obreak and (ef{lneven}) agrees with (ef{g0beven}).
nodes.statement_short: Convert the anti-trace sums into traces of powers, sum with Tr ln, and evaluate determinants via B's eigenvalues and sine/cosine products. For m even the key step is Tr(B^nJ)=Tr(B^n-B'^n).

nodes.name: Strategy via Tr ln
nodes.statement: To derive (\ref{g0bodd}) and (\ref{g0beven}) from (\ref{g0b}), we first convert the final sum, over traces of products of powers of $B$ with $J$, into a sum of traces of pure powers of related matrices, after which the identity \begin{equation} \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n}\mbox{Tr}\,M^n = -\mbox{Tr}\ln(I-M) = -\ln\mbox{Det}(I-M) \end{equation} will allow the sum to be evaluated in terms of the eigenvalues of these related matrices. There are two cases.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the anti-trace sum as traces of powers and use sum Tr M^n/n = -ln Det(I-M).

nodes.name: Trace-log identity
nodes.statement: \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n}\mbox{Tr}\,M^n = -\mbox{Tr}\ln(I-M) = -\ln\mbox{Det}(I-M)
nodes.label: lntr

nodes.name: Case m odd
nodes.statement: \noindent $\bullet$ If $m$ is odd, then the sum in (\ref{g0b}) is over odd powers of $B$. Shuffling indices and using the symmetries of $B$ it can be checked that $B^nJ=(BJ)^n$ for all odd $n$, and so \begin{eqnarray} \ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}&=& \frac{1}{4} \mbox{Tr} \sum_{n\ge 1\atop n {\rm odd}} \frac{1}{n}\left({\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} BJ\right)^n\nonumber\\ &=&\frac{1}{8} \ln\frac{\mbox{Det}\left(1+{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} BJ\right)}{\mbox{Det}\left(1-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} BJ\right)}\,. \end{eqnarray} From (\ref{Jparity}), the eigenvalues of $BJ$ are $(-1)^k\lambda_k$, which for $m$ odd are the numbers $2\cos(2\pi/m)$, $2\cos(4\pi/m)$\,\dots $2\cos((m{-}3)\pi/m)$, all with multiplicity two. Hence \begin{equation} \frac{\mbox{Det}\left(1+{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} BJ\right)}{\mbox{Det}\left(1-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} BJ\right)}= \frac{\cos^4\frac{\pi}{m}\cos^4\frac{2\pi}{m}\cdots\cos^4\frac{(m-3)\pi}{2m}} {\sin^4\frac{\pi}{m}\sin^4\frac{2\pi}{m}\cdots\sin^4\frac{(m-3)\pi}{2m}}\,. \end{equation} To evaluate this we call upon some well-known trigonometric identities. For the numerator we use \begin{equation} \cos\frac{\pi}{n}\cos\frac{2\pi}{n}\cdots\cos\frac{(n-1)\pi}{2n}= \frac{1}{2^{(n-1)/2}}\quad\mbox{for $n$ odd} \end{equation} and for the denominator \begin{equation} \sin\frac{\pi}{n}\sin\frac{2\pi}{n}\cdots\sin\frac{(n-1)\pi}{n}= \frac{n}{2^{n-1}} \end{equation} which implies \begin{equation}\sin^2\frac{\pi}{n}\sin^2\frac{2\pi}{n}\cdots\sin^2\frac{(n-1)\pi}{2n} =\frac{n}{2^{n-1}}\quad\mbox{for $n$ odd.} \end{equation} Using (\ref{trig0}) and (\ref{trig2}), \begin{equation} \frac{\mbox{Det}\left(1+{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} BJ\right)} {\mbox{Det}\left(1-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} BJ\right)}= \frac{1}{m^2}\frac{\sin^4\frac{(m-1)\pi}{2m}}{\cos^4\frac{(m-1)\pi}{2m}} =\left(\frac{4}{m}\frac{\sin^4\frac{(m-1)\pi}{2m}} {\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m}}\right)^2 \end{equation} and so (\ref{lnodd}) is in agreement with (\ref{g0bodd}).
nodes.statement_short: For m odd, B^nJ=(BJ)^n and the determinant ratio is evaluated with trigonometric products.

nodes.name: Odd powers: B^nJ=(BJ)^n
nodes.statement: \noindent $\bullet$ If $m$ is odd, then the sum in (\ref{g0b}) is over odd powers of $B$. Shuffling indices and using the symmetries of $B$ it can be checked that $B^nJ=(BJ)^n$ for all odd $n$, and so \begin{eqnarray} \ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}&=& \frac{1}{4} \mbox{Tr} \sum_{n\ge 1\atop n {\rm odd}} \frac{1}{n}\left({\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} BJ\right)^n\nonumber\\ &=&\frac{1}{8} \ln\frac{\mbox{Det}\left(1+{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} BJ\right)}{\mbox{Det}\left(1-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} BJ\right)}\,. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Write ln g_B as (1/8) ln of a ratio of determinants of 1 +/- BJ/2.

nodes.name: Equation (lnodd)
nodes.statement: \ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}&=& \frac{1}{4} \mbox{Tr} \sum_{n\ge 1\atop n {\rm odd}} \frac{1}{n}\left({\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} BJ\right)^n\nonumber\\ &=&\frac{1}{8} \ln\frac{\mbox{Det}\left(1+{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} BJ\right)}{\mbox{Det}\left(1-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} BJ\right)}\,.
nodes.label: lnodd

nodes.name: Eigenvalues of BJ
nodes.statement: From (\ref{Jparity}), the eigenvalues of $BJ$ are $(-1)^k\lambda_k$, which for $m$ odd are the numbers $2\cos(2\pi/m)$, $2\cos(4\pi/m)$\,\dots $2\cos((m{-}3)\pi/m)$, all with multiplicity two. Hence \begin{equation} \frac{\mbox{Det}\left(1+{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} BJ\right)}{\mbox{Det}\left(1-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} BJ\right)}= \frac{\cos^4\frac{\pi}{m}\cos^4\frac{2\pi}{m}\cdots\cos^4\frac{(m-3)\pi}{2m}} {\sin^4\frac{\pi}{m}\sin^4\frac{2\pi}{m}\cdots\sin^4\frac{(m-3)\pi}{2m}}\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Insert the eigenvalues of BJ to get a ratio of cos^4 and sin^4 products.

nodes.name: Equation at line 2142
nodes.statement: \frac{\mbox{Det}\left(1+{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} BJ\right)}{\mbox{Det}\left(1-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} BJ\right)}= \frac{\cos^4\frac{\pi}{m}\cos^4\frac{2\pi}{m}\cdots\cos^4\frac{(m-3)\pi}{2m}} {\sin^4\frac{\pi}{m}\sin^4\frac{2\pi}{m}\cdots\sin^4\frac{(m-3)\pi}{2m}}\,.

nodes.name: Trigonometric product identities
nodes.statement: To evaluate this we call upon some well-known trigonometric identities. For the numerator we use \begin{equation} \cos\frac{\pi}{n}\cos\frac{2\pi}{n}\cdots\cos\frac{(n-1)\pi}{2n}= \frac{1}{2^{(n-1)/2}}\quad\mbox{for $n$ odd} \end{equation} and for the denominator \begin{equation} \sin\frac{\pi}{n}\sin\frac{2\pi}{n}\cdots\sin\frac{(n-1)\pi}{n}= \frac{n}{2^{n-1}} \end{equation} which implies \begin{equation}\sin^2\frac{\pi}{n}\sin^2\frac{2\pi}{n}\cdots\sin^2\frac{(n-1)\pi}{2n} =\frac{n}{2^{n-1}}\quad\mbox{for $n$ odd.} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Recall the cosine and sine product identities.

nodes.name: Cosine product identity
nodes.statement: \cos\frac{\pi}{n}\cos\frac{2\pi}{n}\cdots\cos\frac{(n-1)\pi}{2n}= \frac{1}{2^{(n-1)/2}}\quad\mbox{for $n$ odd}
nodes.label: trig0

nodes.name: Sine product identity
nodes.statement: \sin\frac{\pi}{n}\sin\frac{2\pi}{n}\cdots\sin\frac{(n-1)\pi}{n}= \frac{n}{2^{n-1}}
nodes.label: trig

nodes.name: Equation (trig2)
nodes.statement: \sin^2\frac{\pi}{n}\sin^2\frac{2\pi}{n}\cdots\sin^2\frac{(n-1)\pi}{2n} =\frac{n}{2^{n-1}}\quad\mbox{for $n$ odd.}
nodes.label: trig2

nodes.name: Conclude m odd
nodes.statement: Using (\ref{trig0}) and (\ref{trig2}), \begin{equation} \frac{\mbox{Det}\left(1+{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} BJ\right)} {\mbox{Det}\left(1-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} BJ\right)}= \frac{1}{m^2}\frac{\sin^4\frac{(m-1)\pi}{2m}}{\cos^4\frac{(m-1)\pi}{2m}} =\left(\frac{4}{m}\frac{\sin^4\frac{(m-1)\pi}{2m}} {\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m}}\right)^2 \end{equation} and so (\ref{lnodd}) is in agreement with (\ref{g0bodd}).
nodes.statement_short: The determinant ratio gives the m-odd closed form.

nodes.name: Equation at line 2166
nodes.statement: \frac{\mbox{Det}\left(1+{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} BJ\right)} {\mbox{Det}\left(1-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} BJ\right)}= \frac{1}{m^2}\frac{\sin^4\frac{(m-1)\pi}{2m}}{\cos^4\frac{(m-1)\pi}{2m}} =\left(\frac{4}{m}\frac{\sin^4\frac{(m-1)\pi}{2m}} {\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m}}\right)^2

nodes.name: Case m even
nodes.statement_short: For m even use the trace identity, then the eigenvalues of B and B'.

nodes.name: Even powers
nodes.statement: \noindent $\bullet$ If $m$ is even, then the sum in (\ref{g0b}) is instead over even powers of $B$.
nodes.statement_short: For m even the sum runs over even powers of B.

nodes.name: Trace identity and its proof
nodes.statement: This time we make use of the identity, valid for $m$ even, that \begin{equation} \mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)=\mbox{Tr}(B^n-B^{\prime n}) \end{equation} where $B^{\prime}$ is the $(m-3)\times(m-3)$ matrix which only differs from $B$ in the following elements: \begin{equation} B^{\prime}_{\frac{m-2}{2},\frac{m-4}{2}}= B^{\prime}_{\frac{m-2}{2},\frac{m}{2}}=0. \end{equation} To prove this identity we write the LHS as \begin{equation} \mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)= B_{i_1i_2}B_{i_2i_3}\cdots B_{i_{n-1}i_{n}}B_{i_{n}m-i_1-2} \end{equation} and note the following properties of $B$: \begin{eqnarray} B_{i,i-1}&=&B_{i,i+1}, \mbox{\quad all other entries $0$;} \\ B_{ij}&=&B_{m-2-i,m-2-j}\,.  \end{eqnarray} The first of these means that (\ref{Banti}) can be interpreted as a weighted sum over all $n$-step paths on the $A_{m-3}$ Dynkin diagram which start and finish at pairs of conjugate nodes $i_1$ and $m{-}2{-}i_1$, $i_1=1\dots m{-}3$, and move by one link at each step. Likewise $\mbox{Tr}(B^n)$ and $\mbox{Tr}(B'^n)$ are weighted sums over $n$-step paths on the same Dynkin diagram, but which this time start and finish at the same node $i_1$, where again $i_1$ is summed from $1$ to $m{-}3$. These observations imply that both sides of (\ref{Banti}) are zero for $n$ odd, and so from now on we can take $n$ to be even (which is the case of direct interest in the current context). Due again to (\ref{B0}), a term in $\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)$ with $i_1<\frac{m-2}{2}$ must include the element $B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m}{2}}$, and a term with $i_1>\frac{m-2}{2}$ must include the element $B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m-4}{2}}$. Assume first that $i_1<\frac{m-2}{2}$, and consider \begin{equation} B_{i_1i_2}B_{i_2i_3}\cdots B_{i_{n-1}i_{n}}B_{i_{n},m-2-i_1} \end{equation} for some particular $i_2\dots i_n$. Suppose $B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m}{2}}$ appears for the final time at $B_{i_pi_{p+1}}$, which means that $B_{i_{p+1}i_{p+2}}=B_{\frac{m}{2}\frac{m+2}{2}}$. By (\ref{B1}), the value of (\ref{Bterm}) is unchanged if all indices $i_q$ with $q>p$ are replaced by their conjugates $m-2-i_q$. The resulting term appears in the trace not of $B^nJ$, but of $B^n$. Similarly, every term in the expansion of $\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)$ with $i_1>\frac{m-2}{2}$ can be equated with a term in the expansion of $\mbox{Tr}(B^n)$ with $i_1>\frac{m-2}{2}$\,. Finally, the terms in the expansions of $\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)$ and $\mbox{Tr}(B^n)$ with $i_1=\frac{m-2}{2}$ are already equal, since $i_1$ is then equal to $m-2-i_1$. Thus $\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)$ is equal to the sum of the terms in the trace of $B^n$ that include either $B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m}{2}}$ or $B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m-4}{2}}$ at least once. Now the trace of $B'^n$ as defined by (\ref{BPdef}) is equal to the trace of $B^n$ minus the terms where $B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m}{2}}$ or $B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m-4}{2}}$ appears at least once. Hence $\mbox{Tr}(B^n-B^{\prime n})$ gives the required terms and (\ref{traceident}) holds.
nodes.statement_short: State and prove Tr(B^nJ)=Tr(B^n-B'^n).

nodes.name: Trace identity for m even
nodes.statement: This time we make use of the identity, valid for $m$ even, that \begin{equation} \mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)=\mbox{Tr}(B^n-B^{\prime n}) \end{equation} where $B^{\prime}$ is the $(m-3)\times(m-3)$ matrix which only differs from $B$ in the following elements: \begin{equation} B^{\prime}_{\frac{m-2}{2},\frac{m-4}{2}}= B^{\prime}_{\frac{m-2}{2},\frac{m}{2}}=0. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For m even, Tr(B^nJ)=Tr(B^n-B'^n), where B' zeroes two entries of the middle row of B.

nodes.name: Trace identity Tr(B^nJ)=Tr(B^n-B'^n)
nodes.statement: \mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)=\mbox{Tr}(B^n-B^{\prime n})
nodes.label: traceident

nodes.name: Proof of the trace identity
nodes.statement: To prove this identity we write the LHS as \begin{equation} \mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)= B_{i_1i_2}B_{i_2i_3}\cdots B_{i_{n-1}i_{n}}B_{i_{n}m-i_1-2} \end{equation} and note the following properties of $B$: \begin{eqnarray} B_{i,i-1}&=&B_{i,i+1}, \mbox{\quad all other entries $0$;} \\ B_{ij}&=&B_{m-2-i,m-2-j}\,.  \end{eqnarray} The first of these means that (\ref{Banti}) can be interpreted as a weighted sum over all $n$-step paths on the $A_{m-3}$ Dynkin diagram which start and finish at pairs of conjugate nodes $i_1$ and $m{-}2{-}i_1$, $i_1=1\dots m{-}3$, and move by one link at each step. Likewise $\mbox{Tr}(B^n)$ and $\mbox{Tr}(B'^n)$ are weighted sums over $n$-step paths on the same Dynkin diagram, but which this time start and finish at the same node $i_1$, where again $i_1$ is summed from $1$ to $m{-}3$. These observations imply that both sides of (\ref{Banti}) are zero for $n$ odd, and so from now on we can take $n$ to be even (which is the case of direct interest in the current context). Due again to (\ref{B0}), a term in $\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)$ with $i_1<\frac{m-2}{2}$ must include the element $B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m}{2}}$, and a term with $i_1>\frac{m-2}{2}$ must include the element $B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m-4}{2}}$. Assume first that $i_1<\frac{m-2}{2}$, and consider \begin{equation} B_{i_1i_2}B_{i_2i_3}\cdots B_{i_{n-1}i_{n}}B_{i_{n},m-2-i_1} \end{equation} for some particular $i_2\dots i_n$. Suppose $B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m}{2}}$ appears for the final time at $B_{i_pi_{p+1}}$, which means that $B_{i_{p+1}i_{p+2}}=B_{\frac{m}{2}\frac{m+2}{2}}$. By (\ref{B1}), the value of (\ref{Bterm}) is unchanged if all indices $i_q$ with $q>p$ are replaced by their conjugates $m-2-i_q$. The resulting term appears in the trace not of $B^nJ$, but of $B^n$. Similarly, every term in the expansion of $\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)$ with $i_1>\frac{m-2}{2}$ can be equated with a term in the expansion of $\mbox{Tr}(B^n)$ with $i_1>\frac{m-2}{2}$\,. Finally, the terms in the expansions of $\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)$ and $\mbox{Tr}(B^n)$ with $i_1=\frac{m-2}{2}$ are already equal, since $i_1$ is then equal to $m-2-i_1$. Thus $\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)$ is equal to the sum of the terms in the trace of $B^n$ that include either $B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m}{2}}$ or $B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m-4}{2}}$ at least once. Now the trace of $B'^n$ as defined by (\ref{BPdef}) is equal to the trace of $B^n$ minus the terms where $B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m}{2}}$ or $B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m-4}{2}}$ appears at least once. Hence $\mbox{Tr}(B^n-B^{\prime n})$ gives the required terms and (\ref{traceident}) holds.
nodes.statement_short: Read the traces as weighted path sums on the A_{m-3} Dynkin diagram; reflecting a path after its last crossing of the middle node matches Tr(B^nJ) with the terms of Tr(B^n) through the middle entries.

nodes.name: Write traces as index sums
nodes.statement: To prove this identity we write the LHS as \begin{equation} \mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)= B_{i_1i_2}B_{i_2i_3}\cdots B_{i_{n-1}i_{n}}B_{i_{n}m-i_1-2} \end{equation} and note the following properties of $B$: \begin{eqnarray} B_{i,i-1}&=&B_{i,i+1}, \mbox{\quad all other entries $0$;} \\ B_{ij}&=&B_{m-2-i,m-2-j}\,.  \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Write Tr(B^nJ) as an index sum and record the properties of B.

nodes.name: Equation (Banti)
nodes.statement: \mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)= B_{i_1i_2}B_{i_2i_3}\cdots B_{i_{n-1}i_{n}}B_{i_{n}m-i_1-2}
nodes.label: Banti

nodes.name: Equation (B0)
nodes.statement: B_{i,i-1}&=&B_{i,i+1}, \mbox{\quad all other entries $0$;}
nodes.label: B0

nodes.name: Path-sum interpretation
nodes.statement: The first of these means that (\ref{Banti}) can be interpreted as a weighted sum over all $n$-step paths on the $A_{m-3}$ Dynkin diagram which start and finish at pairs of conjugate nodes $i_1$ and $m{-}2{-}i_1$, $i_1=1\dots m{-}3$, and move by one link at each step. Likewise $\mbox{Tr}(B^n)$ and $\mbox{Tr}(B'^n)$ are weighted sums over $n$-step paths on the same Dynkin diagram, but which this time start and finish at the same node $i_1$, where again $i_1$ is summed from $1$ to $m{-}3$.
nodes.statement_short: Traces become weighted sums over n-step paths on the A_{m-3} Dynkin diagram.

nodes.name: Reduce to n even
nodes.statement: These observations imply that both sides of (\ref{Banti}) are zero for $n$ odd, and so from now on we can take $n$ to be even (which is the case of direct interest in the current context).
nodes.statement_short: Both sides vanish for n odd, so take n even.

nodes.name: Paths cross the middle
nodes.statement: Due again to (\ref{B0}), a term in $\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)$ with $i_1<\frac{m-2}{2}$ must include the element $B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m}{2}}$, and a term with $i_1>\frac{m-2}{2}$ must include the element $B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m-4}{2}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Terms off the middle must use the middle-row entries of B.

nodes.name: Reflection after the last crossing
nodes.statement: Assume first that $i_1<\frac{m-2}{2}$, and consider \begin{equation} B_{i_1i_2}B_{i_2i_3}\cdots B_{i_{n-1}i_{n}}B_{i_{n},m-2-i_1} \end{equation} for some particular $i_2\dots i_n$. Suppose $B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m}{2}}$ appears for the final time at $B_{i_pi_{p+1}}$, which means that $B_{i_{p+1}i_{p+2}}=B_{\frac{m}{2}\frac{m+2}{2}}$. By (\ref{B1}), the value of (\ref{Bterm}) is unchanged if all indices $i_q$ with $q>p$ are replaced by their conjugates $m-2-i_q$. The resulting term appears in the trace not of $B^nJ$, but of $B^n$. Similarly, every term in the expansion of $\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)$ with $i_1>\frac{m-2}{2}$ can be equated with a term in the expansion of $\mbox{Tr}(B^n)$ with $i_1>\frac{m-2}{2}$\,.
nodes.statement_short: Reflecting indices after the last crossing maps each term of Tr(B^nJ) to a term of Tr(B^n).

nodes.name: Middle starting node
nodes.statement: Finally, the terms in the expansions of $\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)$ and $\mbox{Tr}(B^n)$ with $i_1=\frac{m-2}{2}$ are already equal, since $i_1$ is then equal to $m-2-i_1$.
nodes.statement_short: Terms starting at the middle node already agree.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Thus $\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)$ is equal to the sum of the terms in the trace of $B^n$ that include either $B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m}{2}}$ or $B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m-4}{2}}$ at least once. Now the trace of $B'^n$ as defined by (\ref{BPdef}) is equal to the trace of $B^n$ minus the terms where $B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m}{2}}$ or $B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m-4}{2}}$ appears at least once. Hence $\mbox{Tr}(B^n-B^{\prime n})$ gives the required terms and (\ref{traceident}) holds.
nodes.statement_short: Tr(B'^n) removes exactly the terms through the middle entries, giving the identity.

nodes.name: Sum the series
nodes.statement: If $m$ is even we therefore have \begin{eqnarray} \ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}&=& \sum_{n>1\atop n~{\rm even}} \frac{1}{n2^{n+2}}\mbox{Tr}\,(B^nJ)\nonumber \\ &=&\frac{1}{4} \sum_{n>1\atop n~{\rm even}} \frac{1}{n}\mbox{Tr}\left(\left({\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} B\right)^n-\left({\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} B^{\prime}\right)^n\right)\nonumber\\ &=&\frac{1}{8}\ln \frac{\mbox{Det}\left(I-\frac{1}{4}(B^{\prime})^2\right)} {\mbox{Det}\left(I-\frac{1}{4}B^2\right)} \end{eqnarray} using (\ref{lntr}).
nodes.statement_short: ln g_B becomes (1/8) ln of a ratio of determinants of I - B'^2/4 and I - B^2/4.

nodes.name: Equation (lneven)
nodes.statement: \ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}&=& \sum_{n>1\atop n~{\rm even}} \frac{1}{n2^{n+2}}\mbox{Tr}\,(B^nJ)\nonumber \\ &=&\frac{1}{4} \sum_{n>1\atop n~{\rm even}} \frac{1}{n}\mbox{Tr}\left(\left({\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} B\right)^n-\left({\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} B^{\prime}\right)^n\right)\nonumber\\ &=&\frac{1}{8}\ln \frac{\mbox{Det}\left(I-\frac{1}{4}(B^{\prime})^2\right)} {\mbox{Det}\left(I-\frac{1}{4}B^2\right)}
nodes.label: lneven

nodes.name: Eigenvalues of B'
nodes.statement: To find the eigenvalues of $B'$, $\mbox{Det}(B'-\lambda I)$ can be expanded about the middle row to see that the characteristic polynomial of $B'$ is proportional to $\lambda$ times the product of the (equal) characteristic polynomials of the upper-left and lower-right $(m{-}4)/2\times (m{-}4)/2$ submatrices of $B'$, which we denote $B'_1$ and $B'_2$. These submatrices can be fully diagonalised using the $(m{-}4)/2$ eigenvectors $\psi_k$ of $B$ with $k$ odd: from (\ref{Jparity}), these eigenvectors satisfy $J\psi_k=-\psi_k$. Hence their middle components are zero, while the neighbouring two are the negatives of each other. Given the definition (\ref{BPdef}) of $B'$ this means that projecting each $\psi_k$ for $k$ odd onto its first $(m{-}4)/2$ components yields $(m{-}4)/2$ independent eigenvectors of $B'_1$ with eigenvalues $\lambda_k$, and likewise for $B'_2$. Hence the eigenvalues of $B'$ are \begin{equation} \lambda_k=2\cos\bigl(\frac{\pi k}{m}\bigr)\,,\qquad k=3,5\dots m{-}3\,, \end{equation} each with multiplicity $2$, together with $0$. If $m=2$ mod $4$, then $0$ is also in the set (\ref{elist}), and so the algebraic multiplicity of the zero eigenvalue is $3$, even though its geometric multiplicity turns out to be only $2$. However, this lack of full diagonalisability makes no difference to the computations of traces.
nodes.statement_short: Expanding about the middle row and using the odd-k eigenvectors of B gives the eigenvalues of B'.

nodes.name: Equation (elist)
nodes.statement: \lambda_k=2\cos\bigl(\frac{\pi k}{m}\bigr)\,,\qquad k=3,5\dots m{-}3\,,
nodes.label: elist

nodes.name: Conclude m even
nodes.statement: We can now calculate $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}$. Evaluating (\ref{lneven}) using the eigenvalues just obtained, \begin{eqnarray} \frac{\mbox{Det}\left(I-\frac{1}{4}(B^{\prime})^2\right)} {\mbox{Det}\left(I-\frac{1}{4}B^2\right)}&=& \frac{\sin^4\frac{3\pi}{m}\sin^4\frac{5\pi}{m}\cdots \sin^4\frac{(m-3)\pi}{m}}{\sin^2\frac{2\pi}{m}\sin^2 \frac{3\pi}{m}\cdots\sin^2\frac{(m-2)\pi}{m}}\nonumber\\ &=&\frac{\sin^2\frac{3\pi}{m}\sin^2\frac{5\pi}{m}\cdots \sin^2\frac{(m-3)\pi}{m}}{\sin^2\frac{2\pi}{m}\sin^2 \frac{4\pi}{m}\cdots\sin^2\frac{(m-2)\pi}{m}}\,. \end{eqnarray} Labelling the final numerator $X$ and the denominator $Y$, (\ref{trig}) at $n=m$ and $n=m/2$ respectively implies that \begin{equation} XY=\frac{1}{\sin^4\frac{\pi}{m}}\left(\frac{m}{2^{m-1}}\right)^2~,\qquad Y=\frac{m^2}{2^{m}}\,. \end{equation} Hence \begin{equation} \frac{X}{Y}=\frac{\mbox{Det}\left(I-\frac{1}{4}(B^{\prime})^2\right)} {\mbox{Det}\left(I-\frac{1}{4}B^2\right)}= \left(\frac{2}{m\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m}}\right)^2 \end{equation} \nobreak and (\ref{lneven}) agrees with (\ref{g0beven}).
nodes.statement_short: Evaluate the determinant ratio with the sine product identity to get the m-even closed form.

nodes.name: Equation (frac1)
nodes.statement: \frac{\mbox{Det}\left(I-\frac{1}{4}(B^{\prime})^2\right)} {\mbox{Det}\left(I-\frac{1}{4}B^2\right)}&=& \frac{\sin^4\frac{3\pi}{m}\sin^4\frac{5\pi}{m}\cdots \sin^4\frac{(m-3)\pi}{m}}{\sin^2\frac{2\pi}{m}\sin^2 \frac{3\pi}{m}\cdots\sin^2\frac{(m-2)\pi}{m}}\nonumber\\ &=&\frac{\sin^2\frac{3\pi}{m}\sin^2\frac{5\pi}{m}\cdots \sin^2\frac{(m-3)\pi}{m}}{\sin^2\frac{2\pi}{m}\sin^2 \frac{4\pi}{m}\cdots\sin^2\frac{(m-2)\pi}{m}}\,.
nodes.label: frac1

nodes.name: Equation at line 2310
nodes.statement: XY=\frac{1}{\sin^4\frac{\pi}{m}}\left(\frac{m}{2^{m-1}}\right)^2~,\qquad Y=\frac{m^2}{2^{m}}\,.

nodes.name: Equation at line 2315
nodes.statement: \frac{X}{Y}=\frac{\mbox{Det}\left(I-\frac{1}{4}(B^{\prime})^2\right)} {\mbox{Det}\left(I-\frac{1}{4}B^2\right)}= \left(\frac{2}{m\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m}}\right)^2
